definition_zh: 伸展；延伸；拉紧
definition_en: to reach out your body, to spread over an area or time, or to pull something tight
core_image: 一个人双臂向上伸开，身体被拉得又长又直
scene: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。 She stretched after getting out of bed.
sceneCN: 这里 stretch 是「伸展」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她起床后伸了个懒腰。

derivatives.zh: 有弹性的
担架

senses.title: Reach out the body
senses.definition: to extend your arms, legs, or body
senses.definitionCN: 伸开手臂、腿或身体
senses.example: She stretched after getting out of bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。
senses.why: This is the body making itself long.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体把自己拉长。

senses.title: Spread over an area
senses.definition: to continue over a distance or period
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上延续
senses.example: The fields stretch for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 田野绵延数英里。
senses.why: The body's reach becomes the land's reach.
senses.whyCN: 身体的伸展变成了土地的伸展。

senses.title: Pull tight
senses.definition: to pull something so that it becomes tight or longer
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拉紧或拉长
senses.example: They stretched the rope across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把绳子拉过河面。
senses.why: Here the pulling is done to an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里，拉的动作落在物体上。

intro.en: Stretch comes from Old English streccan, to extend.
intro.cn: stretch 来自古英语 streccan，意为伸展。

items.en: Streccan meant to extend or reach out.
items.cn: streccan 意为伸展或伸出。

items.en: The root meant straight and stretched.
items.cn: 这个词根含有「直」与「拉长」之意。

items.en: Strecchen kept the sense of reaching.
items.cn: 中古英语 strecchen 仍指伸展。

items.en: Land and time could stretch too.
items.cn: 土地与时间也可以「延伸」。

items.en: At a stretch meant without a break.
items.cn: at a stretch 固定为连续不断之意。

note.en: Stretch is compared with look-alike words and with words for extending.
note.cn: 把 stretch 与形近词以及表示延伸的词作比较。

entries.definition: pressure or worry
entries.definitionCN: 压力

entries.definition: a town road
entries.definitionCN: 街道

entries.definition: to mark with something sharp
entries.definitionCN: 抓；划

entries.definition: to make longer or wider
entries.definitionCN: 延伸

entries.definition: to stretch out toward something
entries.definitionCN: 伸手够

entries.definition: to grow larger
entries.definitionCN: 扩大

normalIntro.en: Stretch is length made on purpose, in a body, a road, or a rope.
normalIntro.cn: stretch 是刻意制造出来的长度，在身体、道路或绳子上都一样。

normal.en: Stretch your arms above your head.
normal.cn: 把手臂举过头顶伸展。

normal.en: The beach stretches along the coast.
normal.cn: 海滩沿着海岸延伸。

normal.en: We stopped to stretch our legs.
normal.cn: 我们停下来活动腿脚。

normal.en: He stretched the rubber band.
normal.cn: 他把橡皮筋拉长。

normal.en: She worked for hours at a stretch.
normal.cn: 她连续工作了好几个小时。

abstract.en: A stretch is a promise to become longer.
abstract.cn: 伸展，是一个变长的承诺。

abstract.en: Roads stretch because people need to arrive.
abstract.cn: 道路延伸，因为人需要抵达。

abstract.en: A stretched truth is thinner than it looks.
abstract.cn: 被拉长的事实，比看上去更薄。

examples.en: She stretched after getting out of bed.
examples.cn: 她起床后伸了个懒腰。

examples.en: The fields stretch for miles.
examples.cn: 田野绵延数英里。

examples.en: They stretched the rope across the river.
examples.cn: 他们把绳子拉过河面。

dict_mnemonic.text: stretch 的核心是「拉长」；身体拉长是伸展，土地拉长是延伸，绳子拉长是拉紧，说连续数小时就是 at a stretch。

root: 来自古英语 streccan（伸展、伸出），属日耳曼语词，与「直」的概念相关；由身体的伸展，扩展到空间与时间的绵延，再指把物体拉紧拉长。

sensesIntro.en: Stretch is a body reaching out, land or time continuing, or a rope pulled tight.
sensesIntro.cn: stretch 是身体伸出去、土地或时间延续下去，或绳子被拉紧。

core.en: Two arms opening wide above a waking body.
core.cn: 刚醒的身体上方张开两条手臂。

branches.en: A sleeper yawns and opens the arms.
branches.cn: 睡醒的人打着哈欠张开手臂。

branches.en: A road runs to the horizon.
branches.cn: 一条路一直伸到天边。

branches.en: A rope grows taut between two posts.
branches.cn: 绳子在两根柱子之间绷紧。

branches.en: The body learns length from the land.
branches.cn: 身体从土地那里学会了长度。

branches.en: Too much pulling can break what stretches.
branches.cn: 拉得太狠，会把伸展的东西拉断。

intro.en: Stretch takes verb endings and builds adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: stretch 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: a bed for carrying the sick
items.example: They carried him on a stretcher.
She stretched out on the sofa.
items.exampleCN: 她在沙发上伸展开身体。
我们去活动活动腿脚吧。

definition_zh: 运输；运送；交通工具；运输系统；使激动
definition_en: to carry goods or people from one place to another, or the system that does so
core_image: 一艘货船把集装箱从这片海搬到那片海
scene: 货运码头凌晨装卸完毕，集装箱被吊上开往外地的卡车： The truck driver waited at the port all day just to transport fresh vegetables to the city market on time.
sceneCN: 这里 transport 是动词「运输」（第 1 个义项：把货物运往他处）；句意是司机把蔬菜运到市区市场。

pos.zh: 运输；交通工具；运输系统

collocations.zh: 仿佛置身另一个世界；心驰神往

derivatives.zh: 由 transport 加 -ation 构成，义为「运输；运输系统」
由 transport 加 -er 构成，义为「运输者；运输车」
由 transport 加 -able 构成，义为「可运输的」

senses.title: To carry people or goods from place to place
senses.definition: to take people or goods from one place to another in a vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 用交通工具把人或货物从一地带到另一地
senses.example: The railway transports coal from the north to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路把煤炭从北方运往海岸。
senses.why: The core image is Latin ferre: a load carried across land or sea.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象正是拉丁语 ferre：货物被携过山海。

senses.title: A system or vehicle for moving people and goods
senses.definition: vehicles or a whole system used for moving people and goods
senses.definitionCN: 用于运送人与货物的车辆或整个体系
senses.example: The city needs better public transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市需要更好的公共交通。
senses.why: The act of carrying names both the vehicles and the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 「搬运」这一行为同时命名了车辆与整个网络。

senses.title: To fill someone with strong emotion
senses.definition: to make someone feel extremely happy or excited
senses.definitionCN: 使某人极度喜悦或激动
senses.example: She was transported with joy at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到消息，她欣喜若狂。
senses.why: Emotion lifts the heart as if carried away to another place.
senses.whyCN: 情感把心「搬」走，仿佛去了别处。

senses.title: To send a criminal overseas as punishment
senses.definition: to send a criminal abroad as a former legal punishment
senses.definitionCN: 旧时把罪犯流放海外的刑罚
senses.example: Convicts were once transported to distant colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 罪犯曾被流放到遥远的殖民地。
senses.why: The same carrying across, done to a body and against its will.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「搬运过界」，只是对象是人且违背其意愿。

intro.en: Transport comes from Latin transportare, to carry across, from trans- (across) plus portare (to carry). English took the noun stress in front and the verb stress behind.
intro.cn: transport 来自拉丁语 transportare「搬运过去」：trans-（跨越）+ portare（搬运）。英语名词重音在前，动词重音在后。

items.en: portare meant to carry, seen in port and portable.
items.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为「搬运」，见于 port 与 portable。

items.en: transportare meant to carry across or remove.
items.cn: 拉丁语 transportare 意为「搬过去、移走」。

items.en: Borrowed into English for carrying goods and feelings alike.
items.cn: 进入英语时兼指运送货物与激荡情感。

items.en: The penal sense of sending convicts overseas was common.
items.cn: 17–18 世纪流放罪犯的刑罚义很常见。

items.en: Now centred on moving people, goods, and systems.
items.cn: 现代用法集中于人员、货物的运送及运输系统。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to transport, and words in the carrying field.
note.cn: 与 transport 形近音近的词，以及同属「搬运」义场的词。

entries.definition: the American term for transport systems
entries.definitionCN: （美）运输；运输系统，transport 的名词派生

entries.definition: a vehicle or device that transports
entries.definitionCN: 运输车；运输者，transport 的施动名词

entries.definition: able to be carried
entries.definitionCN: 便携的，与 transport 共享 portare（搬运）词根

entries.definition: to hold and move something
entries.definitionCN: 携带；搬运，最普通的说法

entries.definition: to take or communicate
entries.definitionCN: 运送；传达，偏正式

entries.definition: the act of passing through
entries.definitionCN: 通行；运输途中，强调过程

entries.definition: goods sent together
entries.definitionCN: 一批货运，强调货物本身

normalIntro.en: Keep the two stresses: TRANSport is the thing, transPORT is the act.
normalIntro.cn: 记住双重音：TRANSport 是名词（交通工具），transPORT 是动词（运送）。

normal.en: trans- + port: carry across
normal.cn: trans（跨）+ port（搬运）＝运送

normal.en: collocation: public transport
normal.cn: 常用搭配 public transport（公共交通）

normal.en: portable, porter share the root
normal.cn: portable（便携）、porter（搬运工）同根

normal.en: noun TRANSport, verb transPORT
normal.cn: 名词重音前，动词重音后

normal.en: transported with joy = wildly happy
normal.cn: transported with joy＝欣喜若狂（旧用法）

abstract.en: A freight ship sliding containers across the sea
abstract.cn: 货轮载着集装箱滑过大海

abstract.en: Buses and trains knitting a city together
abstract.cn: 公交与列车把一座城市缝合起来

abstract.en: A melody lifting your heart clean out of the room
abstract.cn: 一段旋律把心提出房间之外

examples.en: Bikes are a cheap way to transport goods across town.
examples.cn: 骑自行车是把货物运过城区的省钱办法。

examples.en: Public transport here runs all night during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间这里的公共交通通宵运行。

examples.en: The music transported the audience to another world.
examples.cn: 音乐让观众仿佛置身另一个世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹死破它」——运输就是把货物踹上车，轰隆隆「破它」一路碾过去：trans（过）+ port（搬运）→ transport。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ portare（搬运）→ transportare「搬过去」。portare 同根词还有 portable、porter。

sensesIntro.en: From carrying loads across the sea to naming the whole system, and even lifting the heart away.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把货物搬过山海」到命名整个系统，甚至把人心也搬走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ship carrying containers across the sea
core.cn: 核心意象：货轮载着集装箱横越大海

branches.en: goods or people carried to a destination
branches.cn: 货物或人被运抵目的地

branches.en: the vehicles and networks that do it
branches.cn: 承担运送的车辆与网络

branches.en: hearts carried away by emotion
branches.cn: 被情感「搬走」的心

branches.en: one act of carrying names both verb and system
branches.cn: 同一次搬运同时命名了动词与系统

branches.en: the old law carried convicts across the sea too
branches.cn: 旧律法也把罪犯「搬」过大洋

intro.en: Transport pairs the prefix trans- with the Latin portare family of carrying words.
intro.cn: transport 由前缀 trans- 与拉丁语 portare（搬运）词族组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare also gave portable, porter, and export.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare 还派生了 portable、porter 与 export。

items.meaning: to carry out of a country

definition_zh: 点；小圆点；小数点；加点；点缀；准时
definition_en: a small round mark, the decimal point, to mark or spread over an area, or exactly on time
core_image: 地图上几个墨点，把散落的村庄连成一条路
scene: 地图上的村庄只剩几个墨点，山路细得像线。 The child joined the dots to draw a house.
sceneCN: 这里 dot 是「小圆点」（第 1 个义项：用笔点出或印在纸上的小圆痕）；句意是孩子把那些点连起来画成了一座房子。

collocations.zh: 给字母 i 加点；把细节弄妥

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「带点的；点状的」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「有点怪的；不很清醒的」（非正式）
由本词加 com 构成，义为「网络公司」，源自网址中的点

senses.title: A small round mark
senses.definition: a small round mark made with a pen or printed on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 用笔点出或印在表面的小圆痕
senses.example: Each village is marked with a red dot.
senses.exampleCN: 每个村庄都用一个小红点标出。
senses.why: The earliest sense is the visible speck itself, the smallest mark a pen can leave.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是那个看得见的小痕，是笔能留下的最小记号。

senses.title: The decimal point
senses.definition: the mark used in British English to separate a whole number from its fraction
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中用来分隔整数与小数的记号
senses.example: Write the answer as four point five, with a dot between them.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案写成四点五，中间加一个小数点。
senses.why: A decimal point is literally a dot, so British usage simply calls the mark by its shape.
senses.whyCN: 小数点本来就是一个小圆点，英式用法干脆按形状来称呼这个记号。

senses.title: To mark or spread with dots
senses.definition: to mark something with small round marks, or to be spread over an area in separate places
senses.definitionCN: 用小圆痕标记某物，或分散地散布在一片区域上
senses.example: Small farms dot the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 小农场散布在山坡上。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action: placing dots turns into covering an area with separate small things.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动作：一个一个点的摆放，变成在一片区域散布许多小东西。

senses.title: Exactly on time
senses.definition: used in the phrase on the dot to mean at exactly the stated time
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on the dot，表示正好在所说的时刻
senses.example: The train left at nine on the dot.
senses.exampleCN: 火车九点整开走了。
senses.why: A clock face marks each minute with a dot, so arriving on the dot means landing exactly on that mark.
senses.whyCN: 钟面上每一分钟都由一个点标出，因此 on the dot 就是正好落在那个点上。

intro.en: Dot is a word of uncertain origin, first recorded in English in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: dot 来源不确定，在英语中最早于十七世纪有记录。

items.en: The word appears in the seventeenth century; no earlier history is securely established.
items.cn: 这个词在十七世纪出现，更早的历史没有可靠结论。

items.en: One common suggestion compares Dutch dot, a knot or small bunch, but this is not proven.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与荷兰语 dot（结、小团）相比，但未获证实。

items.en: Early uses name a small mark or a speck on a surface.
items.cn: 早期用法指表面上的小记号或小斑点。

items.en: The verb to dot and the phrase on the dot both became common.
items.cn: 动词 dot 与短语 on the dot 都在这时通行起来。

items.en: Dotted lines and polka dots entered sewing, printing and fashion.
items.cn: 点线与波点在缝纫、印刷与时尚中使用。

items.en: The internet added dot-com, where the dot is the one in a web address.
items.cn: 互联网时代又加上 dot-com，这里的点是网址中的那个点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dot stem; the near-meaning group gathers other small marks.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dot 词干；近义组收的是其他小记号。

entries.definition: Marked with dots or made of dots, as a dotted line.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「带点的、点状的」，如点线。

entries.definition: Informal British word for slightly crazy or eccentric.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，英式口语，义为「有点古怪的、不大清醒的」。

entries.definition: An internet company, named after the dot in a web address.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网络公司」，得名于网址中的点。

entries.definition: A sharp end or a particular position; also a mark in space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「点、位置、尖端」，也指空间中的标记，范围更广。

entries.definition: A round mark that is usually larger or less regular than a dot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斑点」，通常比 dot 更大或更不规则。

entries.definition: A very small piece or mark of dirt or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微粒、小污点」，指极小的脏物或颜色痕迹。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real uncertain history and the places dots actually appear.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用真实的来源不确定之说，以及点实际出现的场合。

normal.en: Dot has no proven origin; Dutch dot is only a comparison, not a source.
normal.cn: dot 没有已证实的来源，荷兰语 dot 只是比较，不是定论。

normal.en: A decimal point is called a dot in British usage because of its shape.
normal.cn: 小数点英式称 dot，就是因为它的形状。

normal.en: On the dot means on the exact minute mark of a clock.
normal.cn: on the dot 指正好落在钟面的那一分钟刻度上。

normal.en: Polka dots are round marks repeated all over a fabric.
normal.cn: 波点就是布满布面的重复圆点。

normal.en: Farms that dot a hillside look like separate marks on a map.
normal.cn: 散布在山坡上的农场，看起来就像地图上的一个个点。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling on paper and staying round.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落在纸上，保持着圆形。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of dots that a pencil turns into an outline.
abstract.cn: 想象一张点阵纸，被铅笔画出一条轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a clock hand landing exactly on a tiny mark.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面的指针正好落在一个小点上。

examples.en: Put a dot beside the correct answer.
examples.cn: 在正确答案旁边点一个点。

examples.en: The valley is dotted with small stone houses.
examples.cn: 山谷里散布着一座座石头小屋。

examples.en: She arrived at eight on the dot.
examples.cn: 她八点整到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「大特」——笔尖在纸上特地点一下，留下一个特别小的圆痕，就是 dot。

root: dot 于十七世纪出现于英语，来源不确定；荷兰语 dot（结、小团）只是常被拿来比较的形式，不能确定为来源。早期指表面上的小记号，后产生动词「加点、散布」义与 on the dot（准时）等说法。

sensesIntro.en: One small mark becomes a decimal point, a way of spreading things over a map, and a clock mark for punctuality.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个小记号，变成小数点、在地图上散布事物的方式，以及衡量准时的钟面刻度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few ink dots that a line of pencil joins into a shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个墨点被铅笔线连成一个形状。

branches.en: THE MARK: the first sense is the visible speck made by a pen.
branches.cn: 记号线：第一个义项是笔留下的可见小痕。

branches.en: THE DECIMAL: the second sense is the same shape used in numbers.
branches.cn: 小数线：第二个义项是同一形状用在数字里。

branches.en: THE SCATTER: the third sense spreads small marks across a whole area.
branches.cn: 散布线：第三个义项把许多小记号铺到一整片区域。

branches.en: THE MINUTE: the fourth sense uses the clock's dots to mean exactness.
branches.cn: 分刻线：第四个义项用钟面上的点表示精确。

branches.en: A single dot and a landscape full of dots are the same shape seen close and far.
branches.cn: 单个点与满布景色的点，是同一形状的近看与远看。

intro.en: Dot has no Latin root; its family is built with English suffixes and compounds.

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate of dot is known, so the Latin entry list is empty.

definition_zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直（口语夸张用法）
definition_en: in a literal sense or word for word, in fact, or, informally, as a strong intensifier with little literal truth
core_image: 手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母移过去
scene: 朋友把一句玩笑当成真话，还认真追问细节，旁边的人忍不住笑。 She took his joke literally and began checking the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 literally 是「按字面」（第 1 个义项：照词语本义理解）；句意是她把玩笑按字面当真，开始核对数字。画面里可抓住的动作：朋友认真追问、旁人的笑、纸上待核对的数字。

pos.zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 littera（字母）加 -al 构成，指字面的、照字面理解的
由 literal 加 -ness 构成，指拘泥字面的性质
由 literal 加 -ism 构成，指拘泥字面、字面主义的做法

senses.title: In the literal sense of the words
senses.titleCN: 按字面：照词语本来的意思
senses.definition: in the ordinary, literal meaning of the words used, rather than in a figurative or exaggerated one
senses.definitionCN: 按所用词语的本义去理解，而不是按比喻或夸张的意思
senses.example: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet, so literally begins as 'according to the letters': you read what the words actually say, and no picture is allowed to stand in for them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 littera（字母）之上，literally 的起点是「按照字母」：你读的是词语实际写出的内容，不许任何比喻顶替它。

senses.title: Word for word
senses.definition: word for word, following the exact order and wording of the original
senses.definitionCN: 逐字照原话的顺序与措辞，不作改动
senses.example: The contract was translated literally, so the jokes disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 合同是逐字翻译的，所以笑话全没了。
senses.why: If you follow the letters one by one, you also follow the words in their original order; translation done this way keeps the surface and loses the idiom.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个字母一个字母地跟着走，也就按原来的顺序跟着词走；这样翻译保住了表面，却丢掉了习语。

senses.title: In fact, really
senses.titleCN: 确实地：强调事情真的发生
senses.definition: actually, really, without exaggeration, used to stress that something surprising is true
senses.definitionCN: 确实、真的，不带夸张，用来强调某件令人意外的事是真的
senses.example: The team literally ran out of paper on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在最后一天确实把纸用完了。
senses.why: Because 'according to the letters' means 'according to the facts as stated', the adverb can certify a statement: what sounds like an exaggeration is being claimed as plain truth.
senses.whyCN: 既然「按字面」就是「按写明的事实」，这个副词就能为陈述作证：听起来像夸张的话，其实是在说大实话。

senses.title: As an intensifier, almost
senses.titleCN: 口语夸张用法：简直、几乎（并不字面）
senses.definition: used in informal speech as a strong intensifier, often when the statement is not literally true
senses.definitionCN: 口语中作强烈的加强词，常用于所述并非字面真实的情况
senses.example: I literally died laughing at that video.
senses.exampleCN: 那个视频简直把我笑死了。
senses.why: Intensifiers wear out and are borrowed from stronger words; speakers reached for literally to mark emphasis, and the very word for exactness became a badge of exaggeration, a usage dictionaries now record.
senses.whyCN: 加强词会磨损，于是从更有力的词里借用；说话人抓来 literally 表示强调，结果这个专管精确的词反倒成了夸张的标记，词典如今已收录这种用法。

intro.en: Literally is an English adverb built on literal, which descends from Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet.
intro.cn: literally 是英语副词，建立在 literal 之上，而 literal 源自拉丁语 littera（字母）。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural litterae it could mean a letter, a document, or learning.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数 litterae 可指书信、文书或学问。

items.en: Late Latin litteralis meant 'of letters' and described meaning that stays with the written words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 litteralis 意为「字母的」，用来描述紧贴字面文字的涵义。

items.en: English took literal in the fifteenth century for meaning that follows the letter rather than the spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入 literal，指跟随字面而非精神的理解。

items.en: Literally was formed with -ly soon after, first for word-for-word rendering and then for stating plain fact.
items.cn: literally 随后由 -ly 构成，先表逐字表达，再表陈述直白的事实。

items.en: In the twentieth century the intensifier use spread in speech, and it is now recorded, though still criticised in formal writing.
items.cn: 二十世纪里，加强语气的用法在口语中扩散，如今已被收录，但在正式写作中仍有争议。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for letter; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of exactness and reality.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」词干上的词；近义组收表示精确与真实的副词。

normalIntro.en: Literal comes from a Latin noun for a letter, so the adverb is a word about reading the letters in front of you.
normalIntro.cn: literal 来自拉丁语中表示字母的名词，所以这个副词是一个关于「读眼前字母」的词。

normal.en: Literal comes from littera, a letter, so a literal reading stays with the letters in front of you.
normal.cn: literal 来自 littera（字母），所以字面阅读就是紧跟着眼前的字母。

normal.en: Add -ly and the adjective becomes the adverb that says how the reading is done.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，形容词就变成说明「怎样读」的副词。

normal.en: Translate literally is word for word; translate freely is by sense, and the two labels mark opposite choices.
normal.cn: 逐字翻译是跟着词走，意译是跟着意思走，两个说法标出相反的选择。

normal.en: Literally true certifies a surprising fact, so the word is doing the work of really.
normal.cn: literally true 是在为一件意外的事实作证，这个词在做 really 的活。

normal.en: A sentence like I literally died is not literal at all, which shows the intensifier has drifted from its root.
normal.cn: 像「我简直死了」这样的句子一点也不是字面意思，可见这个加强词已经漂离了词根。

abstract.en: A word built on letters becomes a word for truth, and then for emphasis, and the direction of travel is worth noticing.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在字母上的词变成了表示真实的词，又变成加强词，这个移动方向值得注意。

abstract.en: Exactness is a surface; when a sentence is read only at the surface, the joke or the metaphor is lost.
abstract.cn: 精确只是表面；只按表面读一句话，玩笑或隐喻就丢了。

abstract.en: The strongest claim of literalness can end up producing the least literal sentence.
abstract.cn: 最卖力声称字面的一句话，可能恰恰最不字面。

definition_zh: 第一；首先；第一点
definition_en: used to introduce the first in a list of points, reasons, or arguments
core_image: 排队报数的人举起第一根手指：接下来还要一条一条往下数
scene: 答辩现场，她清了清嗓子，翻开笔记本宣布要讲三条理由。 Firstly, the design saves energy; secondly, it costs less.
sceneCN: 这里 firstly 是「第一；首先」（第 1 个义项：用于列举中的第一点）；句意为：她宣布理由时先用 firstly 开头，表明后面还有第二条、第三条。

pos.zh: 第一；首先（用于列举第一点）

forms.label: 说明
forms.form: adverb only; no comparative form in common use

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「第一的；最初的」，firstly 由其加 -ly 构成
基础词副词用法，义为「首先；先于他人」，常与 firstly 互换
first（第一）+ born（出生），义为「头生的；长子长女的」
first（第一）+ hand（手），义为「直接的；第一手的」
fore（前）+ most（最），义为「最重要的；最前的」，与 firstly 的列举功能相关

senses.title: To introduce the first point in a list
senses.titleCN: 第一；首先（列举中的第一点）
senses.definition: used to begin the first item when you are going to mention several items one by one
senses.definitionCN: 当你准备逐条列出若干要点时，用来引出第一条
senses.example: Firstly, I would like to thank everyone who helped with the project.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，我要感谢所有为这个项目提供帮助的人。
senses.why: The word is first plus the adverb ending -ly, so it literally means doing something in the first place.
senses.whyCN: firstly 由 first（第一）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面意思就是「处在第一位地」，于是专门用于开启列举。

senses.title: To signal order before other points follow
senses.titleCN: 提示顺序；预告还有下文
senses.definition: used to tell the listener that more points are coming after this one
senses.definitionCN: 用来告诉听者：这条之后还有更多要点，请按顺序听
senses.example: There are two reasons why I disagree. Firstly, the data is outdated.
senses.exampleCN: 我不同意有两个原因。第一，数据已经过时了。
senses.why: Because firstly only marks position one, its very use promises a secondly or thirdly to come.
senses.whyCN: firstly 只标记「第一位」，所以它一出现就暗示后面会有「第二」「第三」，起到预告顺序的作用。

senses.title: To open a formal argument or explanation
senses.definition: used in formal speech or writing to organize an argument in clear steps
senses.definitionCN: 在正式口头或书面表达中，用来把论述分成清晰的步骤
senses.example: The report firstly examines the causes of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告首先考察了危机的成因。
senses.why: Formal writing favors explicit ordering words, and firstly makes the first step visible to the reader.
senses.whyCN: 正式文体偏爱显性的顺序标记，firstly 把「第一步」明确摆在读者面前，使论述结构一目了然。

senses.title: To rank the most important reason first
senses.titleCN: 把最重要的理由放在第一
senses.definition: used to put the weightiest point at the head of a list for emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 把最关键的一点放在列表最前面，以示强调
senses.example: Firstly and above all, safety must come before speed.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，也是最重要的：安全必须排在速度之前。
senses.why: Putting a point in first position naturally marks it as primary, so firstly can carry emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 被放在「第一位」的要点天然带有首要性，因此 firstly 也可以承载强调功能。

senses.title: To replace first in enumerated speech
senses.titleCN: 替代 first 作列举副词
senses.definition: used instead of first when first might be read as an adjective or noun
senses.definitionCN: 在 first 可能被误读为形容词或名词时，用它明确副词身份
senses.example: Firstly, check the power supply before touching the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 第一，先检查电源，然后再碰机器。
senses.why: The -ly ending makes the adverbial role unambiguous, which is why some writers prefer it.
senses.whyCN: -ly 后缀让副词身份毫无歧义，这正是部分作者在列举时更愿意用 firstly 的原因。

senses.title: To open a summary or recap
senses.definition: used to begin restating previously made points in order
senses.definitionCN: 在结尾按顺序复述先前要点时作开头用
senses.example: To conclude, firstly we agreed on the budget, and then on the timeline.
senses.exampleCN: 总结一下：第一，我们敲定了预算；然后敲定了时间表。
senses.why: Recaps reuse the original order of the list, so the first restated point is again marked firstly.
senses.whyCN: 复述沿用原本的列举顺序，被放在第一位的要点再次用 firstly 标记。

senses.title: To structure spoken instructions
senses.definition: used when giving step-by-step spoken directions or procedures
senses.definitionCN: 口头给出一步步的操作指引或流程时使用
senses.example: Firstly, open the lid, then pour in the rice.
senses.exampleCN: 第一步，先打开锅盖，然后倒入大米。
senses.why: Procedures are lists of actions, and the first action naturally gets the first marker.
senses.whyCN: 操作流程就是动作清单，第一个动作自然配上「第一」这个标记。

senses.title: To mark the first of paired contrasts
senses.titleCN: 标记成对对照中的前者
senses.definition: used to present the first side of a two-part comparison or contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于呈现两部分对比中的前一部分
senses.example: The plan has strengths and weaknesses. Firstly, it is cheap to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划有利有弊。第一，它运营成本低。
senses.why: Contrast also works as an ordered list, so the first item still receives firstly.
senses.whyCN: 对比本质上也是一种有顺序的列举，前一项同样由 firstly 来标记。

intro.en: Firstly is a transparent English formation: the adverb ending -ly added to first, an old Germanic ordinal.
intro.cn: firstly 是一个构成透明的英语词：在古老的日耳曼语序数词 first 后面加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: The root behind first is generally reconstructed as *per-, *pre- meaning forward or before, seen in related forms across many Indo-European languages.
items.cn: 一般认为 first 的词根可重构为 *per-、*pre-，意为「向前；在前」，在多个印欧语的同源词中可见。

items.en: The comparative form *frumizon and related superlative forms developed in Germanic, giving Old English forms such as fyrmest and fyrst, meaning earliest or foremost.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中发展出比较级形式 *frumizon 及相关最高级形式，古英语由此产生 fyrmest、fyrst 等词形，义为「最早的；最前的」。

items.en: By the ninth century, fyrst was established as the superlative of fore, meaning before, so first literally means most before, that is, earliest.
items.cn: 到九世纪，fyrst 已确立为 fore（在前）的最高级，所以 first 的字面义是「最在前」，即「最早」。

items.en: Firstly is first recorded in the sixteenth century; earlier English writers typically used first alone as the list-opening adverb.
items.cn: firstly 最早见于十六世纪的记载；更早的英语作者通常只用 first 兼作列举副词。

items.en: Since the eighteenth century, usage commentators have debated whether firstly is necessary, since first does the same job; both remain in common formal use today.
items.cn: 自十八世纪以来，用法评论者一直争论 firstly 是否必要，因为 first 也能承担同样功能；如今两者在正式语体中都很常用。

items.en: Firstly is common in British formal writing, while American style guides often prefer first; the choice is stylistic rather than grammatical.
items.cn: firstly 在英式正式书面语中常见，而美式风格指南多偏好 first；这种选择属于文体偏好，而非语法问题。

note.en: Watch out for the near-identical first, which can do the same job, and for other ordering adverbs that continue the list.
note.cn: 注意与它几乎同义的 first（同样可用于列举开头），以及继续往下列举的其他顺序副词。

entries.definition: ordinal number and adverb meaning before all others; can replace firstly in lists
entries.definitionCN: 序数词兼副词，义为「第一；最先」，在列举中可替代 firstly

entries.definition: adjective or noun for the child born earliest in a family
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，指家中最早出生的孩子，与 firstly 共享 first 词根

entries.definition: adverb meaning in a firm or steady way; spelled similarly but from firm, not first
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「坚定地；牢固地」，拼写与 firstly 相近，但词根是 firm 而非 first

entries.definition: adverb introducing the second point in a list, usually after firstly or first
entries.definitionCN: 引出列举中第二点的副词，通常紧跟 firstly 或 first 之后

entries.definition: adverb meaning at the beginning, often describing a starting state rather than a list position
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初；开始时」，多描述起始状态而非列举位置

entries.definition: phrase used to open the first point, more conversational than firstly
entries.definitionCN: 用于引出第一点的短语，比 firstly 更口语化

normalIntro.en: Five down-to-earth ways to lock firstly into memory using its real building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 五个基于真实构词的接地气方法，帮你把 firstly 记牢。

normal.en: Split it: first + ly, meaning in the first way or in first place.
normal.cn: 拆开记：first + ly，即「以第一的方式；在第一位」。

normal.en: Pair it with secondly: wherever firstly appears, a secondly is waiting in line.
normal.cn: 与 secondly 配对记：firstly 一出现，secondly 就在后面排队。

normal.en: Recall first means most before, so firstly means speaking from the most-before position.
normal.cn: 联想 first 的本义「最在前」，firstly 就是「从最前面的位置说起」。

normal.en: Practice the set: firstly, secondly, thirdly — a counting chant for arguments.
normal.cn: 练三连：firstly、secondly、thirdly——给论点报数的小口诀。

normal.en: Contrast with initially: initially means at the start of time, firstly means at the head of a list.
normal.cn: 与 initially 对比记：initially 指「时间上的起初」，firstly 指「列表中的第一

abstract.en: Picture a queue of arguments at a ticket window; the one holding ticket number one shouts firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象一排论点在售票窗口排队，手里拿一号票的那个喊出 firstly。

abstract.en: See an index finger pointing at line one of your notes, tapping twice: that tap is firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象食指指着笔记第一行敲两下：那两下敲击就是 firstly。

abstract.en: Feel a relay race where the first runner must hand off the baton; her start signal is firstly.
abstract.cn: 想象接力赛第一棒必须交出接力棒，她的起跑信号就是 firstly。

examples.en: Firstly, let me outline the three problems we identified.
examples.cn: 首先，让我概述我们发现的三个问题。

examples.en: The essay firstly introduces the theory, then applies it to real cases.
examples.cn: 文章首先介绍理论，然后将其应用于真实案例。

examples.en: She opened the meeting with a short greeting.
examples.cn: 她以简短的问候开始了会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛斯得利」——佛祖先「斯」得「利」：佛祖也讲究先来后到，第一份好处归排在第一位的人，所以 firstly 就是「第一；首先」。

root: firstly 由古英语序数词 first（源自 fore「在前」的最高级 fyrst，义为「最早；最前」）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面义为「以第一的位置」。词根可追溯至原始印欧语的 *per-、*pre-（向前；在前），属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: From its transparent build, first plus -ly, firstly spreads from marking the first list item into ordering, emphasis, and structured speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 从 first 加 -ly 的透明构造出发，firstly 由「标记列表第一项」扩展到顺序提示、强调功能和结构化表达。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at the head of a queue of points, holding ticket number one
core.cn: 核心意象：站在一排论点的队首，手里攥着一号票

branches.en: introducing the first item and clarifying its adverb role
branches.cn: 引出第一项并明确其副词身份

branches.en: promising more points to come and structuring contrasts
branches.cn: 预告后文并组织对比结构

branches.en: organizing formal arguments and spoken procedures
branches.cn: 组织正式论述与口头流程

branches.en: ranking the weightiest reason in first place
branches.cn: 把最重要的理由排在首位

branches.en: reopening a summary in the original order
branches.cn: 按原顺序开启总结复述

intro.en: Firstly is built from the ordinal first plus the adverbial suffix -ly; related words show how first branches into a family.
intro.cn: firstly 由序数词 first 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；相关词展示出 first 如何派生出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Firstly itself is Germanic in origin, but Latin cousins that express before and first show the shared Indo-European idea.
latinIntro.cn: firstly 本身源自日耳曼语，但拉丁语中表达「在前；第一」的同族词体现了共同的印欧观念。

items.example: firstly = first + ly, in the first place
items.exampleCN: firstly 即 first 加 ly，义为「在第一位地」

items.example: the first step is the hardest

items.exampleCN: 预见、预言中的 fore- 即此前缀
prepare、predict 中的 pre- 与 first 同源于「在前」的观念

derivatives.zh: 第一的；最初的
头生的；长子长女的
最重要的；最前的

definition_zh: 平原；朴素的；简单的；不加修饰的；坦率的
definition_en: a large flat area of land, or simple without decoration, or clear and direct
core_image: 一片没有任何起伏和装饰的平地——同样平坦的还有衣料、话语和食物
scene: 火车驶出丘陵，窗外忽然展开一望无际的大平原。 We crossed the vast plain in less than an hour.
sceneCN: 这里是「平原」（第 1 个义项：大片平坦的陆地）；句意为不到一小时我们就穿过了辽阔的平原。画面就是那片平得望不到边的土地。

pos.zh: 朴素的；简单的；坦率的；不加奶的

derivatives.zh: plain 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「朴素地； plainly 明白地」
plain 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「朴素；平易」
plain 与 spoken 合成，义为「说话直率的」

senses.title: A large flat area of land
senses.definition: a wide area of flat land with few trees
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有树木的大片平地
senses.example: Buffalo once covered the American plains.
senses.exampleCN: 野牛曾经遍布美洲大平原。
senses.why: Latin planus described flatness, and the land sense kept the most literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 planus 指平坦，土地义保留了最字面的意思。

senses.title: Without decoration
senses.definition: simple and without ornament or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 简单而没有任何装饰或花纹
senses.example: She wore a plain grey dress to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了条素净的灰裙子去面试。
senses.why: A flat surface carries no carving or colour, so flatness became visual simplicity.
senses.whyCN: 平的表面没有雕饰与色彩，平坦便成了视觉上的简朴。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: easy to understand because it is stated directly
senses.definitionCN: 因为说得直接而易于理解
senses.example: Keep the instructions plain and short.
senses.exampleCN: 说明要写得简单明了。
senses.why: An uncluttered surface is easy to see across, so the image slid to uncluttered meaning.
senses.whyCN: 没有遮挡的表面一眼望穿，意象便滑向了不绕弯子的意思。

senses.title: Direct and honest in speech
senses.definition: saying exactly what is thought, without politeness padding
senses.definitionCN: 把想法原样说出，不加客套粉饰
senses.example: To be plain with you, the plan will fail.
senses.exampleCN: 直说吧，这个计划会失败。
senses.why: Flatness applied to words means no decorated curves, only the straight line of truth.
senses.whyCN: 平坦用于话语即没有装饰的曲线，只有真理的直线。

senses.title: Ordinary, not special
senses.definition: ordinary and not beautiful or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 普通而不漂亮、不惊人的
senses.example: He's a plain man with plain habits.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个长相普通、习惯平常的人。
senses.why: No decoration and no surprise leaves only the ordinary, so plain slid to unremarkable.
senses.whyCN: 没有装饰也没有意外，只剩平常，plain 便滑向「不起眼」。

senses.title: Without milk or sugar
senses.definition: food or drink with nothing added, especially without milk
senses.definitionCN: 什么都没加的食物或饮料，尤指不加奶
senses.example: I take my coffee plain.
senses.exampleCN: 我喝咖啡什么都不加。
senses.why: The bare surface again: nothing poured, sprinkled or stirred into it.
senses.whyCN: 又是那个光秃秃的表面：什么都没倒进去、撒进去、搅进去。

intro.en: Plain is Latin planus, flat, that reached English twice — once through French for the adjective and noun, and once as the word plain itself.
intro.cn: plain 来自拉丁语 planus（平的），经法语两次进入英语——形容词名词走一条路，同源词另有走法。

items.en: Planus meant flat or level, spreading on the ground.
items.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为平的、水平的，向地面铺展。

items.en: Old French plain and plein carried flatness and also fullness, the two cousins of one root.
items.cn: 古法语 plain 与 plein 兼有「平」与「满」两义，同根兄弟。

items.en: The word entered English with the flat-land sense and the clear, unadorned sense together.
items.cn: 该词进入英语时便同时带着平地义与清楚、不加修饰义。

items.en: The land sense kept the spelling plain, while the fullness sense settled as plain and the plane of geometry.
items.cn: 土地义沿用 plain 拼法，而「满」义与几何的平面分道为 plane。

items.en: Today plain covers land, dress, speech, food and the humble ordinary face.
items.cn: 今天 plain 覆盖土地、衣着、话语、饮食与平凡的面孔。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the planus family; the near-meaning group gathers flatness and directness.
note.cn: 形近组收 planus 词族；近义组收平坦与直率词。

entries.definition: A flat surface, a tool or an aircraft; the twin spelling that split from plain.
entries.definitionCN: 平面、刨子或飞机；与 plain 分道而来的孪生拼法。

entries.definition: A flat stretch of highland, or a stage where progress stops.
entries.definitionCN: 高原，或进步停滞的平台期。

entries.definition: To make something flat and clear to the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事在头脑中摊平、说清楚。

entries.definition: Easy and basic, without complexity of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 容易而基本，没有任何复杂成分。

entries.definition: Level and lacking emotion or fizz; the physical twin of plain.
entries.definitionCN: 平的、乏味的；plain 的物理孪生词。

entries.definition: Direct to the point of rudeness in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 直率到近乎无礼。

normalIntro.en: One Latin root, one picture: something laid flat, with nothing added.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁词根、一幅画：被摊平的东西，什么也没添加。

normal.en: Planus, plain, plane: flatness wearing three costumes.
normal.cn: planus、plain、plane：平坦穿着三套戏服。

normal.en: A plain is flat land; plain clothes is a flat, undecorated outfit.
normal.cn: plain 是平地；plain clothes 是无装饰的衣服。

normal.en: In plain English means words spread out flat where all can read them.
normal.cn: in plain English 是把话摊平，人人能读。

normal.en: Plain yogurt carries the bare surface into the fridge.
normal.cn: plain yogurt 把光秃秃的表面带进冰箱。

normal.en: To be plain with you flattens every curve out of the sentence.
normal.cn: to be plain with you 把句子里的每条弯都压直。

abstract.en: Grass running to the horizon with not a single hill to break it.
abstract.cn: 草地一直跑到地平线，没有一座山丘打断。

abstract.en: A grey dress with no buttons, no lace, no shine.
abstract.cn: 一条灰裙，没有纽扣、没有花边、没有光泽。

abstract.en: A sentence with all decoration stripped off, standing like a bare plank.
abstract.cn: 一句话被剥掉所有装饰，像一块光板立着。

examples.en: The farmhouse stood alone on the wide plain.
examples.cn: 农舍孤零零立在广阔的平原上。

examples.en: She gave us the plain facts, without comfort.
examples.cn: 她把无情的事实直说了，没有安慰。

examples.en: He prefers plain yogurt to the sweetened kind.
examples.cn: 比起加糖的，他更喜欢原味酸奶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺累嗯」——平平地铺到累嗯，一马平川；plain 就是平原、朴素。

root: plain 源自拉丁语 planus（平坦的），经古法语 plain/plein 进入英语；「平」义引申出平原、朴素、直率等义；与 plane、plateau、explain 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Latin flatness grows into a prairie, an unadorned dress, a direct sentence, an ordinary face and a cup of coffee with nothing added.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语的平坦长成一片草原、一件素裙、一句直话、一张平常的脸和一杯什么都没加的咖啡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat surface with nothing added and nothing hidden.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个平坦的表面，没加任何东西，也没有任何遮挡。

branches.en: the prairie to the horizon
branches.cn: 延伸到地平线的草原

branches.en: the dress with no ornament
branches.cn: 没有任何饰物的裙子

branches.en: the sentence that walks straight
branches.cn: 径直走来的那句话

branches.en: the face no one describes twice
branches.cn: 没人想多描述一次的脸

branches.en: from clear words to bare coffee
branches.cn: 从明白话到清咖啡

intro.en: Plain's family is the Latin root planus in many costumes, joined by English suffixes.
intro.cn: plain 的词族是拉丁词根 planus 的多套戏服，再加英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root planus also lives in plateau, plane, explain and plan.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 planus 还活在 plateau、plane、explain 与 plan 里。

latinEntries.meaning: an English derivative of the headword
latinEntries.meaningCN: plain 加 -ly 构成，义为「朴素地；明白地」

latinEntries.meaning: an English derivative of the headword
latinEntries.meaningCN: plain 加 -ness 构成，义为「朴素」

definition_zh: 康复；恢复；找回；追回；镇定下来
definition_en: to become healthy again; to return to a former condition; to get back something lost; to regain control of oneself
core_image: 病床上的人扶着床沿，第一次站起来
scene: 病床上的病人扶着床沿，慢慢把脚放到地上。 He slowly recovered from the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 recovered 是「康复」（第 1 个义项：恢复健康）；句意为他在手术后慢慢康复。画面里可留意：扶住床沿的手、落到地上的脚。

derivatives.zh: 康复；恢复；找回
可恢复的
已恢复的

senses.title: To become healthy again
senses.definition: to return to health after an illness or an operation
senses.definitionCN: 在生病或手术后恢复健康
senses.example: He slowly recovered from the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 他在手术后慢慢康复。
senses.why: The word pictures getting something back, and in illness what is got back is the body's former strength.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描绘「把东西取回」，而在疾病中取回的，是身体原有的力气。

senses.title: To return to a former condition
senses.definition: to return to an earlier good state after a fall or a shock
senses.definitionCN: 在下滑或冲击之后回到先前较好的状态
senses.example: The economy recovered quickly after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后经济迅速恢复。
senses.why: Health, markets, and nations all move away from a good state and then return, so one verb covers every return.
senses.whyCN: 身体、市场与国家都会离开良好状态再回来，因此同一个动词涵盖所有「回来」。

senses.title: To get back something lost
senses.definition: to find or obtain again something that was lost or taken away
senses.definitionCN: 重新找到或取得失去或被拿走的东西
senses.example: She recovered her lost keys from the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 她从沙发里找回了丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to regain possession, and the body recovering health is a special case of getting something back.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是重新获得，而身体恢复健康正是「取回某物」的一个特例。

senses.title: To regain money or losses
senses.definition: to win back money, costs, or losses that had been lost
senses.definitionCN: 把失去的钱、成本或损失重新赢回来
senses.example: The company recovered most of its losses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司追回了大部分损失。
senses.why: In business, what is recovered is value, and the word keeps its accounting sense of making the balance whole again.
senses.whyCN: 在商业中，追回的是价值，这个词保留了让账目重新平衡的会计含义。

senses.title: To regain control of oneself
senses.definition: to become calm and controlled again after strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 在强烈情绪之后重新变得平静自持
senses.example: He recovered himself and continued speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他镇定下来，继续发言。
senses.why: To recover oneself is to get one's own composure back, as if composure were a thing that had slipped away.
senses.whyCN: 「恢复自己」就是把镇定取回来，仿佛镇定是一件滑走的东西。

intro.en: Recover is a Latin verb of regaining that came through French, and its image of getting something back covers health, wealth, and composure.
intro.cn: recover 是经法语传来的拉丁语「重新获得」动词，其「取回」的形象覆盖健康、财富与镇定。

items.en: Recuperare meant to regain or recover, especially what had been lost.
items.cn: recuperare 意为重新获得或收回，尤指失去之物。

items.en: Recuperatio named the act of regaining, the noun behind recovery.
items.cn: recuperatio 指重新获得的行为，是 recovery 背后的名词。

items.en: Old French recovrer carried the verb into English with its broad sense intact.
items.cn: 古法语 recovrer 把这个动词带入英语，宽泛含义完好保留。

items.en: Middle English recoveren covered health, property, and composure.
items.cn: 中古英语 recoveren 已涵盖健康、财产与镇定。

items.en: Modern English extended the verb to markets, data, and personal calm.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词扩展到市场、数据与个人平静。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs beginning with re-; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of healing and regaining.
note.cn: 形近组收以 re- 开头的动词；近义组收表治愈与重新获得的动词。

entries.definition: To cover something again.
entries.definitionCN: 重新覆盖。

entries.definition: To move back suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 突然后退。

entries.definition: To tell a story in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 详细讲述。

entries.definition: To become healthy again.
entries.definitionCN: 痊愈。

entries.definition: To get something back.
entries.definitionCN: 重新获得。

entries.definition: To bring something back.
entries.definitionCN: 取回；找回。

entries.definition: To recover health and strength.
entries.definitionCN: 康复；休养。

normalIntro.en: The word is getting back: health, things, money, and calm are all things that can be lost and regained.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「取回」：健康、物品、金钱与平静，都是可能失去又能重新得到的东西。

normal.en: Re plus cover: to get back what was taken away.
normal.cn: re 加 cover：把被拿走的东西重新取回。

normal.en: Recover from illness, recover losses, recover oneself: one verb, many returns.
normal.cn: recover from illness、recover losses、recover oneself：一个动词，多种「回来」。

normal.en: Recovered is the past form: recover, recovered, recovering.
normal.cn: 过去式是 recovered：recover、recovered、recovering。

normal.en: Fully recover means to return to complete health.
normal.cn: fully recover 意为完全恢复健康。

normal.en: Do not confuse recover with re-cover, which means cover again.
normal.cn: 不要把 recover 与 re-cover 混淆，后者意为重新覆盖。

abstract.en: Recovery is not the absence of loss but the refusal to stay lost.
abstract.cn: 恢复不是没有失去，而是拒绝停留在失去里。

abstract.en: What a person recovers from shows what that person can survive.
abstract.cn: 一个人从什么中恢复过来，显示出他能承受什么。

abstract.en: To recover oneself is the quietest and hardest recovery of all.
abstract.cn: 恢复镇定，是最安静也最艰难的一种恢复。

examples.en: He slowly recovered from the operation.
examples.cn: 他在手术后慢慢康复。

examples.en: She recovered her lost keys from the sofa.
examples.cn: 她从沙发里找回了丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: The company recovered most of its losses.
examples.cn: 这家公司追回了大部分损失。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cover（取得）：把失去的东西重新取回，就是 recover——康复、找回、恢复都由「取回」而来。

root: 拉丁 recuperare（重新获得）→ 古法语 recovrer → 中古英语 recoveren → 英语 recover；同族有 recovery、recoverable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is getting back what was lost; the senses move from health to a former state, lost objects, money, and composure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把失去的取回」；义项从健康，到原有状态、失物、金钱，再到镇定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a patient's hand on the bed rail, feet reaching the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：病人的手扶住床沿，双脚落到地上。

branches.en: a first step from a sickbed
branches.cn: 从病床上迈出的第一步

branches.en: a market rising after a fall
branches.cn: 下跌后回升的市场

branches.en: keys found under a cushion
branches.cn: 在坐垫下找到的钥匙

branches.en: money returned to a ledger
branches.cn: 记回账上的钱

branches.en: a speaker finding his voice again
branches.cn: 重新找回声音的发言者

intro.en: A Latin verb of regaining passes through French, and its noun and adjective offspring name the process and the possibility.
intro.cn: 一个表「重新获得」的拉丁动词经法语传来，其名词与形容词后代分别命名过程与可能性。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recuperare, to regain, with the noun recuperatio behind recovery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recuperare（重新获得），其名词 recuperatio 是 recovery 的来源。

items.meaning: in the process of getting back

definition_zh: 尴尬的；笨拙的；难对付的
definition_en: causing embarrassment, or moving in a clumsy way
core_image: 两只手都不知该往哪儿放，站在门口进退不得
scene: 礼堂里忽然安静下来。 He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
sceneCN: 这里 awkward 是「尴尬的」（第 1 个义项：令人不自在、难为情的）；句意是他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。

pos.zh: 形容词：尴尬的；笨拙的；难对付的

derivatives.zh: 由 awkward 加 -ly 构成，义为「尴尬地；笨拙地」
由 awkward 加 -ness 构成，义为「尴尬；笨拙」

senses.title: Causing embarrassment
senses.definition: causing embarrassment or making people uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 令人难为情或让人不自在的
senses.example: He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。
senses.why: Awkward comes from Old Norse afugr, turned the wrong way, so the core image is something facing backwards and out of place.
senses.whyCN: awkward 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反了」，核心意象是东西朝反了、位置不对。

senses.title: Clumsy in movement
senses.definition: moving or behaving in a clumsy way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或举止笨拙的
senses.example: The puppy was awkward on the smooth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 小狗在光滑的地板上走得很笨拙。
senses.why: A body facing the wrong way moves badly, so the same word names physical clumsiness.

definition_zh: 滥用（权力、制度、药物）；虐待；辱骂；侵害行为；糟蹋、过度使用；辜负（信任）
definition_en: to use something or someone in a wrong, harmful or excessive way, or such wrong use itself
core_image: 一把本该切菜的刀被拿去砍门，刃口卷了，手也划破了
scene: 车间里那台机器早就该保养了，主管却一直让人超负荷地开。 The manager was accused of abusing his power.
sceneCN: 这里的 abusing 是「滥用职权」（第 1 个义项：把权力用在不当的地方）；句意为主管被指滥用权力。画面里有老旧的机器和满脸不服的工人。

pos.zh: 名词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；侵害行为
动词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；糟蹋

senses.title: Misuse of power or authority
senses.definition: the use of power or official authority for the wrong purpose or beyond its proper limits
senses.definitionCN: 把权力或职务上的权限用于错误目的，或超出应有的限度
senses.example: The manager was accused of abusing his power.
senses.exampleCN: 这名主管被指滥用权力。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to use something away from its proper use; power is the first thing people are tempted to use this way.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「把东西用到偏离正当用途的地方」；权力正是人们最容易这样使用的东西，所以它成了第一个义项。

senses.title: Harmful use of drugs or alcohol
senses.definition: the use of drugs, alcohol or other substances in a way that harms the user
senses.definitionCN: 以伤害使用者的方式服用药物、酒精等物质
senses.example: Drug abuse among teenagers has fallen in recent years.
senses.exampleCN: 近年来青少年药物滥用有所减少。
senses.why: A substance is meant to heal or give pleasure in measure; using it outside that measure turns a tool into harm, the same wrong use as before.
senses.whyCN: 药物本来是用来治病或适量取乐的；一旦超出这个度量，工具就变成伤害，这仍是同一个「用错了」的动作。

senses.title: Cruel treatment of a person or animal
senses.definition: cruel or violent treatment of a person or animal, especially one who cannot defend himself or herself
senses.definitionCN: 残忍或暴力地对待人或动物，尤指无法自我保护的弱者
senses.example: The charity runs a hotline for reports of child abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构设有举报虐待儿童的热线。
senses.why: When the thing being used is a living person, wrong use stops being a metaphor: the person is treated as an object, and that is abuse.
senses.whyCN: 当被「使用」的对象是活人时，「用错」不再是比喻：人被当成物件来对待，这就是虐待。

senses.title: Insulting words aimed at someone
senses.definition: spoken words that insult, threaten or humiliate someone repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 反复用来侮辱、威胁或羞辱某人的话语
senses.example: Shouting is one thing, but verbal abuse is not part of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 大声说话是一回事，但言语辱骂不属于工作内容。
senses.why: Speech is also a tool; turned against a person it wounds rather than works, so the same word covers hurtful language.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是一种工具；当它被掉转过来对着人，就不再做事而只造成伤害，于是同一个词也指伤人的话。

senses.title: Exploiting a system or rule
senses.definition: the dishonest use of a system, procedure or rule to gain an advantage it was not meant to give
senses.definitionCN: 不正当地利用制度、程序或规则，取得它本不该给的便利
senses.example: The report found widespread abuse of the visa system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告发现签证制度被广泛钻空子。
senses.why: Systems are tools too; using their gaps instead of their purpose is misuse at the scale of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 制度同样是工具；利用它的缝隙而不是它的用途，就是「用错」在机构层面的表现。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.definition: to damage equipment, a body or a place by using it too roughly or too often
senses.definitionCN: 因使用过于粗暴或频繁而损坏设备、身体或场所
senses.example: He abused the old truck until the engine finally gave out.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那辆旧卡车往死里用，最后发动机彻底坏了。
senses.why: Here the damage is visible: a tool used past its limits wears out, and the word names the wearing rather than the intention.
senses.whyCN: 这里的损坏看得见：工具被用到超出限度就会磨损，这个词于是指磨损本身，而不只是意图。

senses.title: A wrongful act, in the plural
senses.definition: in the plural, cruel or unjust acts, especially those that violate people's rights
senses.definitionCN: 用复数形式，指残忍或不公正的行为，尤指侵犯人权的行为
senses.example: The commission documented human rights abuses in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会记录了该地区的侵犯人权行为。
senses.why: Each single misuse is an event; counted together they become a record of wrongs, which is why the plural names a pattern of harm.
senses.whyCN: 每一次滥用都是一件事；把它们合起来数，就成了一份罪错清单，所以复数形式指的是成串的侵害。

senses.title: To betray the trust placed in you
senses.definition: to take advantage of someone's trust, kindness or hospitality for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 利用别人的信任、善意或款待来为自己谋利
senses.example: She felt he had abused her trust in the worst possible way.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得他以最糟糕的方式辜负了她的信任。
senses.why: Trust is the most invisible thing one person lends another; using it as a means to an end is misuse in its most personal form.
senses.whyCN: 信任是一个人借给另一个人最无形的东西；把它当成手段来用，就是「用错」最私人化的一种形态。

intro.en: Abuse goes back to a Latin verb that simply means to use something wrongly, and every sense keeps that shape.
intro.cn: abuse 可追到拉丁语中一个意为「用错」的动词，所有义项都保持着这个形状。

items.en: Uti meant 'to use, make use of'. It is well recorded, and it is also the source of the English word use through Latin usus.
items.cn: uti 意为「使用、利用」，有明确记录；它经由拉丁语 usus 也是英语 use 的来源。

items.en: Ab- 'away from' plus uti formed abuti, 'to misuse, use up'. The prefix marks use that has turned away from the proper purpose.
items.cn: ab-「离开」与 uti 构成 abuti，意为「误用、用尽」；这个前缀标示用法偏离了正当目的。

items.en: The past participle abusus served both as a noun 'misuse' and as the participle behind the adjective abusivus.
items.cn: 过去分词 abusus 既作名词表示「误用」，也是形容词 abusivus 的分词基础。

items.en: Old French abuser carried both the sense of misusing a thing and of deceiving a person, and English took the word in that double shape.
items.cn: 古法语 abuser 同时带有「误用某物」和「欺骗某人」两种意思，英语正是以这双重的面貌借入的。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the fourteenth century and the verb in the following one; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词在十四世纪有记录，动词晚一个世纪出现；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin uti family; the near-meaning group names wrong use, cruel treatment and insult with different degrees of force.
note.cn: 形近组是拉丁语 uti 词族；近义组列出「用错」「苛待」与「侮辱」，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective describing words or treatment that are cruel, insulting or harmful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辱骂的、虐待的、滥用的」，描述伤人的言语或对待。

entries.definition: A person who treats someone cruelly or uses something wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「施虐者、滥用者」，指苛待他人或不当使用某物的人。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a cruel or insulting manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「辱骂地、虐待地」，由 abusive 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To free someone from a mistaken belief; the prefix dis- reverses the idea of using wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使醒悟、纠正……的错误想法」，与 abuse 同根，前缀 dis- 表示「解除」。

entries.definition: The wrong or careless use of something, especially an object or a system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「误用、滥用」，多指对物品或制度的错误使用，不含虐待义。

entries.definition: To treat a person or animal badly, especially over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「苛待、虐待」，专指对人的恶劣对待，与「滥用权力」无关。

entries.definition: To use someone or something unfairly for your own gain.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「剥削、利用」，强调为自己获利而不公平地使用他人。

entries.definition: To say something rude that offends someone; a single act, unlike repeated verbal abuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「侮辱」，通常指一次性的冒犯，不像 verbal abuse 那样反复发生。

normalIntro.en: These hooks are built on the real Latin pair ab- and uti, and on the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在真实的拉丁语组合 ab- 与 uti 上，并使用这个词的固定搭配。

normal.en: uti is to use, and ab- turns use away from its purpose: abuse is use in the wrong direction.
normal.cn: uti 是「使用」，ab- 把使用从正当目的上转开：abuse 就是「用错了方向」。

normal.en: abuse of power is the phrase used in news reports about officials.
normal.cn: abuse of power 是新闻报道官员问题时常用的说法。

normal.en: drug abuse names the harmful use of a substance, not the substance itself.
normal.cn: drug abuse 指的是对物质的有害使用，而不是物质本身。

normal.en: child abuse and elder abuse both protect people who cannot defend themselves.
normal.cn: child abuse 与 elder abuse 都指向无法自我保护的弱者。

normal.en: Keep the pair abuse and abusive together: the act and the adjective that describes it.
normal.cn: 把 abuse 和 abusive 成对记：一个是行为，一个是形容这种行为的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen knife used to pry open a door: the blade is ruined and the hand is cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一把菜刀被拿去撬门：刀刃毁了，手也划破了。

abstract.en: The word always asks what a thing is for, and then shows it being used against that purpose.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终先问「这东西是干什么用的」，再展示它被用到了相反的方向。

abstract.en: Abuse leaves two marks: the tool is worn out and the person on the other side is hurt.
abstract.cn: 滥用会留下两道痕迹：工具被磨损，另一边的人受了伤。

examples.en: The report describes several abuses of power inside the department.
examples.cn: 报告描述了该部门内部的多起滥用权力行为。

examples.en: She never abused her position to get special treatment.
examples.cn: 她从未滥用职位来获取特殊待遇。

examples.en: Neighbours reported the noise, but what worried them more was the verbal abuse.
examples.cn: 邻居们报告了噪音，但更让他们担心的是那些辱骂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额必优使」——把好东西用歪了，就是不当地使：滥用。

root: 拉丁语 abuti「误用、用尽」，由 ab-「离开」与 uti「使用」构成；其过去分词 abusus 兼作名词「误用」，英语经古法语 abuser 借入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of abuse is a tool turned against its purpose: power, a substance, a person, speech, a system, a machine, a right or a trust.
sensesIntro.cn: abuse 的每个义项都是「工具被掉转过来反对它本来的用途」：权力、物质、人、言语、制度、机器、权利或信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tool meant for one job is used for another and is damaged in the process.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该干一件事的工具被拿去干别的，并在这个过程中被损坏。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC SPHERE: power and rules are steered toward private gain.

definition_zh: 自信；信心；信任；秘密
definition_en: a feeling of trust in yourself or in another person
core_image: 演讲者走上台时背挺得笔直，步子稳稳的
scene: 排练多次之后，她走上台时一点也不慌。 Practice gave her the confidence to speak in public.
sceneCN: 这里 confidence 指「自信」（第 1 个义项：对自己能力的信任）；句意是练习给了她当众讲话的自信。

derivatives.zh: 自信的；有把握的
机密的；私下的
自信地
倾诉；信赖

senses.title: Trust in yourself
senses.definition: a calm belief that you can do something well
senses.definitionCN: 平静地相信自己能把事情做好
senses.example: She answered every question with confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她信心十足地回答了每个问题。
senses.why: Repeated practice turns a shaky hope into steady certainty.
senses.whyCN: 反复练习把摇晃的希望变成稳定的确信。

senses.title: Trust in another person
senses.definition: a feeling that someone or something can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某人或某物可以依靠的感觉
senses.example: I have great confidence in your judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 我非常信任你的判断。
senses.why: Trust is a bet placed on someone else's steadiness.
senses.whyCN: 信任是把赌注押在别人的稳当上。

senses.title: A secret shared privately
senses.definition: a secret told to someone with a promise of silence
senses.definitionCN: 在对方承诺保密的情况下说出的秘密
senses.example: They exchanged confidences late at night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在深夜交换了彼此的秘密。
senses.why: To trust someone with a secret is to lend them part of yourself.
senses.whyCN: 把秘密托付给人，就是把一部分自己借给了对方。

intro.en: Confidence comes from Latin confidentia, a trusting, from confidere, to trust completely.
intro.cn: confidence 来自拉丁语 confidentia，意为信赖，源自 confidere（完全信任）。

items.en: Fidere meant to trust or have faith in someone.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任或对某人抱有信心。

items.en: Confidere added com- to make the trust complete.
items.cn: confidere 加上 com-，表示彻底地信任。

items.en: French confidence named a firm hope or assurance.
items.cn: 法语 confidence 指坚定的希望或把握。

items.en: English confidence first meant reliance on another person.
items.cn: 英语 confidence 最初指对他人的依靠。

items.en: It now also means belief in oneself and a secret told in trust.
items.cn: 如今它也指对自己的信心，以及在信任中吐露的秘密。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same trust family, and the meaning group names other kinds of assurance.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一信任词族的词，近义组列出其他表示把握的说法。

entries.definition: sure about one's own ability
entries.definitionCN: 自信的；有把握的

entries.definition: meant to be kept secret
entries.definitionCN: 机密的

entries.definition: a person you tell private things to
entries.definitionCN: 知己；心腹

entries.definition: a feeling of certainty about something
entries.definitionCN: 把握；保证

entries.definition: the state of being completely sure
entries.definitionCN: 确信；必然

entries.definition: belief that someone is honest and reliable
entries.definitionCN: 信任；信赖

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a steady walk onto a stage, then move to a friend's promise and to a whispered secret.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从稳步走上舞台开始，再走到朋友的承诺与低声说出的秘密。

normal.en: Con- is fully and fid- is trust, so confidence is complete trust, in yourself or in others.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，fid- 是信任，所以 confidence 就是彻底的信任，对自己或对别人。

normal.en: Confidence does not shout; it walks in quietly and sits down.
normal.cn: 自信不会大声喊，它安静地走进来然后坐下。

normal.en: A vote of confidence is other people lending you their trust.
normal.cn: 信任投票，就是别人把他们的信任借给你。

normal.en: Confidence and confidential both come from trust, one is belief and one is a secret.
normal.cn: confidence 与 confidential 都来自信任，一个是相信，一个是秘密。

normal.en: Say a thing in confidence, and it must stay in that room.
normal.cn: 以保密的方式说出一件事，它就必须留在那个房间里。

abstract.en: Picture a straight back and an even step.
abstract.cn: 想象一条笔直的背与均匀的步伐。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake that does not hurry.
abstract.cn: 想象一次不急不忙的握手。

abstract.en: Picture a key handed over with a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙连同承诺一起交出。

examples.en: Practice slowly built her confidence on stage.
examples.cn: 练习慢慢建立起了她在台上的自信。

examples.en: The manager has full confidence in the new team.
examples.cn: 经理对新团队有充分的信心。

examples.en: He told me the news in confidence.
examples.cn: 他私下把这个消息告诉了我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confidence 记成 con（完全）加 fid（信任）加 ence：完全相信自己，是自信；完全相信别人，是信任。

root: 源自拉丁语 confidentia（com 完全 + fidere 信任），本义是完全的信赖，后引申为自信、信任与私下吐露的秘密。

sensesIntro.en: From trust in your own step, to trust placed in another, and finally to a secret kept between two people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对自己步伐的信任，到交给别人的信任，最后到两人之间守住的秘密。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady figure walking on stage, and a key passed quietly to a friend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个稳稳走上台的人，以及一把被悄悄交给朋友的钥匙。

branches.en: Self confidence grows from doing the same thing many times.
branches.cn: 自信来自把同一件事做上许多遍。

branches.en: Confidence in others is a judgement about their reliability.
branches.cn: 对他人的信任，是对其可靠程度的判断。

branches.en: A confidence shared is a secret placed in safe hands.
branches.cn: 被分享的秘密，是放进可靠之手的秘密。

branches.en: Both kinds of confidence are tested only when something goes wrong.
branches.cn: 两种信心都只有在出问题时才真正受到检验。

branches.en: Trust is what lets a secret be told at all.
branches.cn: 正因为信任，秘密才可能被说出口。

intro.en: Confidence is built on Latin com-, fully, plus fidere, to trust, with the noun ending -ence.
intro.cn: confidence 由拉丁语 com-（完全）、fidere（信任）与名词词尾 -ence 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin trust base fid- also appears in fidelity and faith.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的信任词基 fid- 也出现在 fidelity 与 faith 中。

items.exampleCN: 每尝试一次，她的信心就增长一些。

items.example: She walked confidently to the front.

faithfulness to a person or promise

items.exampleCN: 这个团队重视信守承诺。

items.exampleCN: 来电者设下了一个信任骗局。

definition_zh: 假定；承担；呈现
definition_en: to suppose without proof, to take on a duty, or to begin to have a quality
core_image: 一件外套被人直接披到自己身上
scene: 会议没核对数据就开始讨论。 Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
sceneCN: 这里 assume 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：没有证据就先当作成立）；句意是大家都假定这些数字是对的。

derivatives.zh: 名词：假定；承担
形容词：假定的；装出的
连词：假如

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe that something is true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据时先认定某事成立
senses.example: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。
senses.why: Assume comes from Latin assumere, 'to take up', so taking a claim up as your own is to accept it before it has been proved.
senses.whyCN: assume 源自拉丁语 assumere「拿起来」，把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，就是在被证实之前先接受它。

senses.title: Take on a duty
senses.definition: to take on responsibility, power or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过责任、权力或职位
senses.example: She assumed control of the company in June.
senses.exampleCN: 她在六月接管了公司。
senses.why: The literal Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives here: power or duty is picked up and carried by the new holder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的本义在这个义项里保留下来：权力或责任被新的承担者接过去扛起来。

senses.title: Begin to have a quality
senses.definition: to begin to have a particular quality or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 开始带有某种性质或外表
senses.example: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。
senses.why: Putting on an appearance is the same gesture as putting on a coat, so the word can describe a look that something takes on.
senses.whyCN: 把某种外表披到自己身上，与披上一件外套是同一个动作，因此这个词也能说某物呈现出某种样子。

intro.en: Assume is a Latin verb of taking, and every sense keeps something of that gesture.
intro.cn: assume 是拉丁语中表示「拿取」的动词，各个义项都保留着这个动作的影子。

items.en: sumere meant 'to take or take up'.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿、取」。

items.en: assumere meant 'to take to oneself'.
items.cn: assumere 意为「取到自己身上」。

items.en: assumptus was the taking up of a burden or a claim.
items.cn: assumptus 指接过负担或接受某种主张。

items.en: assumer meant 'to take on or claim'.
items.cn: assumer 意为「承担、主张」。

items.en: English added the sense of taking on an appearance.
items.cn: 英语又增出「呈现出某种外表」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sume root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of supposing and taking on.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sume 词根；近义组是表示假定与承担的动词。

entries.definition: to take up again

normalIntro.en: Assume is always a taking: a claim, a duty or a look.
normalIntro.cn: assume 始终是一个「拿」的动作：拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表。

normal.en: The pattern assume that is common in argument.
normal.cn: 论证中常见 assume that 结构。

normal.en: Assume responsibility is the formal way to say take the blame or duty.
normal.cn: assume responsibility 是承担责任的正式说法。

normal.en: The past participle assumed can mean pretended.
normal.cn: 过去分词 assumed 可表示「假装的」。

normal.en: Do not confuse assume with presume, which is based on likelihood.
normal.cn: 不要与 presume 混淆，后者带有「有理由推定」的意味。

normal.en: The s sounds like a soft z in the middle.
normal.cn: 中间的 s 读作近似 z 的浊音。

abstract.en: See a coat lifted from a hook and put on without asking.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套被从钩子上取下，不问自穿。

abstract.en: See a signature on a line that says responsibility.
abstract.cn: 想象在写着「责任」的那一栏签下名字。

abstract.en: See a face turning the colour of the sky before rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸变成雨前天空的颜色。

examples.en: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
examples.cn: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。

examples.en: She assumed control of the company in June.
examples.cn: 她在六月接管了公司。

examples.en: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sume（拿）：把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，是假定；把权力与责任拿过来，是承担；把一副样子披上身，是呈现。

root: 源自拉丁语 assumere「取到自己身上」，由 ad-「向」与 sumere「拿」构成；由「拿过来」引申为未经证实便接受，再引申为承担职责与呈现外表。

sensesIntro.en: Taking a claim, a duty or a look are three objects of the same grasping verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表，是同一个「取」的动作面对三种对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted and placed on oneself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一样东西被拿起并放到自己身上。

branches.en: assume that prices will rise
branches.cn: 假定物价会上涨

branches.en: be assumed to be safe

branches.cn: 接管控制权

branches.cn: 显出一副担忧的神色

intro.en: The root sume, 'to take', runs through consume, resume and presume.
intro.cn: 词根 sume 意为「拿」，贯穿 consume、resume 与 presume。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere is the base, and its compounds spread across daily English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 是词基，它的复合词遍布日常英语。

definition_zh: 分开；部门；除法
definition_en: the act of separating something into parts, a part of a large organization, or the sharing out of something
core_image: 一条走廊把办公楼分成两半，门牌各自挂在两边
scene: 走廊从电梯口一直通到底，左右两边各挂一块门牌。 She works in the sales division.
sceneCN: 这里 division 指「部门」（第 2 个义项：机构里分出的单位）；句意是她在销售部门工作。

senses.title: The act of splitting, or the split itself
senses.definition: the act of separating into parts, or the state of being split into opposing sides
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分开的行为，或分成对立两边的状态
senses.example: The division of the land took years.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地的划分花了好几年。
senses.why: A line drawn once can keep two sides facing each other for a long time.
senses.whyCN: 画下的一条线，能让两边对望很久。

senses.title: A part of an organization
senses.definition: a large unit inside a company or an official body
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构内部的一个大单位
senses.example: She works in the sales division.
senses.exampleCN: 她在销售部工作。
senses.why: A big body divides its work so each part can be watched.
senses.whyCN: 大机构把工作分开，每一块才看得住。

senses.title: The arithmetic of sharing into equal parts
senses.definition: the process of finding how many times one number fits into another
senses.definitionCN: 求一个数里含有另一个数多少次的运算
senses.example: Long division still troubles some students.
senses.exampleCN: 长除法至今让一些学生头疼。
senses.why: Numbers are split as neatly as bread, but with no crumbs.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能像面包一样分开，只是不掉渣。

intro.en: Division is Latin divisio, a parting, from dividere, to force apart.
intro.cn: division 是拉丁语 divisio（分开），来自 dividere（强行拆开）。

items.en: Dividere meant to part what was joined.
items.cn: dividere 指把连在一起的东西分开。

items.en: Divisio named the act and the line it left.
items.cn: divisio 指分开的动作与留下的界线。

items.en: A divisio also meant a share given to an heir.
items.cn: divisio 也指分给继承人的一份。

items.en: English used it for splitting and for shares.
items.cn: 英语借入后指切开与分得的一份。

items.en: Army and trade gave it the sense of a unit.
items.cn: 军队与商业给了它「单位」的意思。

items.en: Today a division can be a sum, a team or a quarrel.
items.cn: 今天一个 division 可以是一道除法、一个团队或一场争执。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the dividere stem, while the meaning group names other kinds of parting.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dividere 这段词干，近义组则是几种分开的名目。

entries.definition: to split or share out

normal.en: Divide plus -ion: the cut has become a lasting line.
normal.cn: divide 加 ion，切开成了留下来的界线。

normal.en: The division between the two teams is only on paper.
normal.cn: 两个组之间的划分只写在纸上。

normal.en: He was moved to the research division last spring.
normal.cn: 去年春天他被调到研究部。

normal.en: A division of opinion delayed the vote.
normal.cn: 意见分歧让表决推迟了。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor cutting a building into two wings.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊把楼切成两翼。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper ruled into equal boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被划成相等的格子。

abstract.en: Picture two queues forming at one wide door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇宽门前排成两队。

examples.cn: 这块地的划分花了三年。

examples.en: Division is easier with a calculator.
examples.cn: 有了计算器，除法容易多了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 division 记成「切开留下的线」：divide 是切，加上名词尾，就成了划分、分出的部门，也算术里的除法。

root: 源自拉丁语 divisio，来自 dividere（强行拆开）。本义是切开以及切开后留下的界线，也指分给继承人的一份。后来在军队与商业中指机构中的一个单位，在算术中指除法。

sensesIntro.en: From a corridor splitting a building to a sum that asks how many fit inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条把楼分开的走廊，到一道问「里面能装几个」的算式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long corridor halving a building, a name plate on each side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长走廊把楼分成两半，两边各挂一块门牌。

branches.en: The first sense is the cut and the line it leaves.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是切开以及留下的界线。

branches.en: The second sense is an official share of a large body.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是大机构里正式分出的一块。

branches.en: The third sense splits numbers instead of rooms.
branches.cn: 第三个义项分的是数字，不是房间。

branches.en: Both senses turn one large thing into named parts.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把一个大东西变成有名字的几块。

intro.en: Division belongs to the dividere family, where one stem serves rooms, offices and arithmetic.
intro.cn: division 属于 dividere 一族，同一个词干同时服务房间、办公室与算术。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere, to force apart, gives division and divide; -ive and -ible pull it towards conflict and numbers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dividere（分开）给出 division 与 divide，后缀 -ive 与 -ible 把它拉向冲突与数字。
