definition_zh: 停止；终止；不再存在
definition_en: to stop happening or doing something, or to come to an end
core_image: 正在转动的轮子被人按住，慢慢停住
scene: 机器发出怪响，工人按下开关。 The noise ceased as soon as the power was cut.
sceneCN: 这里 cease 指「停止」（第 1 个义项：声音不再继续）；句意是电源一断，噪音立刻停止了。

derivatives.zh: 停止；中止
不停的；无休止的
不停地

senses.title: To stop doing or happening
senses.definition: to bring or come to an end, especially of an activity or a sound
senses.definitionCN: 使活动或声音结束，或自身结束
senses.example: The rain ceased at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 雨在半夜停了。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to hold back or delay, and holding something back ends its motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是拦住或拖延，而把某物拦住就是终止它的运动。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.definition: to come to an end as a thing that exists, often used of companies or species
senses.definitionCN: 作为存在物走到尽头，常用于公司或物种
senses.example: The old factory ceased to exist in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老厂在九十年代就不存在了。
senses.why: When an activity stops for ever, the thing that carried it out also stops existing.
senses.whyCN: 当一项活动永久停止，从事这项活动的事物也就不再存在。

intro.en: Cease comes from a Latin verb meaning to delay or hold back, which passed through French into English.
intro.cn: cease 来自一个意为拖延或拦住的拉丁语动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Cessare meant to be slow, to delay or to leave off an activity.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cessare 意为迟缓、拖延或停止某项活动。

items.en: Cesser carried the sense of stopping and yielding into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser 把停止与让出的含义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: Cesen appears in the fourteenth century for leaving off an action.
items.cn: 中古英语 cesen 在十四世纪已指停止某项行动。

items.en: Legal and military phrases such as cease and desist and cease fire become fixed.
items.cn: 停止并终止、停火等法律与军事说法逐渐固定。

items.en: Cease to exist extends the word from actions to the ending of things themselves.
items.cn: cease to exist 把该词从动作扩展到事物本身的终结。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cessation family, while the meaning group lists other verbs for ending.
note.cn: 形近组沿停止词族展开，近义组列出其他表示结束的动词。

entries.definition: a stopping of an activity
entries.definitionCN: 活动的停止

entries.definition: never stopping
entries.definitionCN: 从不停歇的

entries.definition: without a pause
entries.definitionCN: 毫不停顿地

entries.definition: to end movement or action
entries.definitionCN: 结束运动或行动

entries.definition: to stop suddenly, especially marching
entries.definitionCN: 突然停止，尤指行军

entries.definition: to come or bring to a finish
entries.definitionCN: 结束或使结束

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie cease to cessation, to the legal phrase and to the picture of a stopped wheel.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cease 与 cessation、法律短语以及停住的轮子连起来。

normal.en: Cease and cessation share one root, so ending an action and the end itself sit side by side.
normal.cn: cease 与 cessation 同根，停止动作与停止状态并排而立。

normal.en: Cease fire is the shortest way to remember the military use.
normal.cn: cease fire 是记住军事用法最短的方式。

normal.en: Cease to exist puts the word before a verb, a pattern shared with fail to and happen to.
normal.cn: cease to exist 把词放在动词前，与 fail to、happen to 同型。

normal.en: Ceaseless keeps the word but adds -less, so it means without any cease.
normal.cn: ceaseless 保留词干再加 -less，意思就是毫无停止。

normal.en: The spelling has ea but the sound is a long ee, as in peace and please.
normal.cn: 拼写是 ea，读音却是长音 ee，如同 peace 与 please。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy wheel slowing until it stands still.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的轮子慢下来，最后静止。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed on a switch and a sudden silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在开关上，四周忽然安静。

abstract.en: Picture a factory gate rusting shut for the last time.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂大门最后一次生锈地合上。

examples.en: The rain finally ceased in the afternoon.
examples.cn: 雨终于在下午停了。

examples.en: Both sides agreed to cease fire at dawn.
examples.cn: 双方同意在黎明停火。

examples.en: That company ceased to exist years ago.
examples.cn: 那家公司多年前就不存在了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cease 读音像「息死」：气息一停，动作也就停了。

root: 源自拉丁语 cessare（迟缓、停止），经古法语 cesser 进入英语；cessation 与之同根。

sensesIntro.en: Holding something back stops an action, and a permanent stop removes the thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物拦住会让动作停下，而永久的停止则让事物本身消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a turning wheel brought to rest by a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：转动的轮子被一只手按住停下。

branches.en: A sound or activity stops and the word names the moment.
branches.cn: 声音或活动停下，这个词就命名那个时刻。

branches.en: A permanent stop extends to the ending of the thing itself.
branches.cn: 永久停止扩展到事物本身的终结。

branches.en: Cease fire keeps the sense in military commands.
branches.cn: cease fire 把该义保留在军事口令里。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of no further movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「不再有后续运动」的意思。

branches.en: Cease to exist is the formal way to say a thing is gone.
branches.cn: cease to exist 是「事物已消失」的正式说法。

intro.en: Cease forms its family with -less and -ation, and keeps a fixed legal phrase.
intro.cn: cease 用 -less 与 -ation 构成词族，并保留一条固定法律短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare, to delay, also underlies cessation and the legal word cessor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cessare（拖延）也是 cessation 与法律词 cessor 的词根。

items.example: The ceasing of the rain surprised us.
A cessation of fighting was agreed.

items.exampleCN: 无休止的噪音让所有人都累了。

items.example: Cessare is the source of cease.
items.exampleCN: cessare 是 cease 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Cessare passed through French as cesser.

definition_zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的；以理论推理为依据的
definition_en: based on general principles and reasoning rather than on practice, observation or direct experiment
core_image: 黑板上推演到一半的公式，与现实车间里尚未造出的机器隔着一段距离
scene: 理论组把公式钉满白板，实验组在旁摇头。 Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
sceneCN: 这里 theoretical 指「理论的」（第 1 个义项：依据原理与推理、而非实践与实验）；句意：理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。图中可辨识物件：写满推演的黑板、尚未装配的仪器草图。

pos.zh: 理论的；理论上的；假设的（与 practical、experimental、applied 相对）

derivatives.zh: 理论；学说；原理
理论家；理论工作者
理论上；按理说
理论的（多见于 theoretic framework 等学术搭配）
建立理论；作理论推断
定理（与 theory 同出希腊 theōrēma「所观之物」）

senses.title: Based on Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论的：依据原理而非实践
senses.definition: based on ideas and general principles rather than on practice or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 依据观念与一般原理，而非实践或实验的
senses.example: Theoretical physics often runs decades ahead of experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 理论物理学往往比实验领先数十年。
senses.why: Greek theoria named looking and contemplating. The adjective marks knowledge reached by reasoning about principles, not by handling the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 theoria 指观看与沉思。这个形容词标出的是通过对原理的推理而获得的知识，而不是亲手处理事物得来的知识。

senses.title: Hypothetical
senses.titleCN: 假设的：只为推理而设想
senses.definition: imagined or supposed for the purpose of reasoning, not actual
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而设想或假定，并非实际存在
senses.example: Let us take a theoretical case in which nobody pays tax.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们设想一个没人缴税的理论情形。
senses.why: A case built to test an argument is not observed anywhere. It exists only inside the reasoning, so the adjective shifts from 'about theory' to 'merely supposed'.
senses.whyCN: 为检验论证而构造的情形并不在任何地方被观察到，它只存在于推理之中；于是这个形容词从「关于理论的」滑向「仅仅假设的」。

senses.title: Predicted but Unseen
senses.titleCN: 理论预言的：尚未观测到
senses.definition: predicted by theory but not yet observed
senses.definitionCN: 由理论预言、但尚未被观测到的
senses.example: The theoretical particle would leave only a tiny trace in the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这种理论粒子只会在探测器中留下极微小的痕迹。
senses.why: Theory can name something before any instrument sees it. The adjective marks that priority of reasoning over observation, which is common in particle physics.
senses.whyCN: 理论可以在任何仪器看见某物之前先给它命名；这个形容词标出的正是推理先于观测，这在粒子物理中很常见。

senses.title: Of the Theory Branch
senses.titleCN: 理论分支的：学科的理论侧
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of a subject that studies principles rather than applications
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究原理而非应用的那个学科分支
senses.example: She holds a chair in theoretical computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任理论计算机科学方向的教授。
senses.why: Disciplines split into theory and application. The adjective labels the theory side, where the aim is to prove what is possible, not to ship a product.
senses.whyCN: 学科会分成理论与应用两侧；这个形容词标出理论一侧，其目标是证明什么在原理上可行，而不是交付产品。

senses.title: Idealized Model
senses.titleCN: 理想化模型的：删去复杂细节
senses.definition: belonging to an idealized model that leaves out complicating details
senses.definitionCN: 属于省略了复杂细节的理想化模型
senses.example: The theoretical model assumes a perfectly smooth sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论模型假定球体完全光滑。
senses.why: A model is made by leaving things out. The word marks that the object is a construction, so its predictions hold only as far as the omissions are harmless.
senses.whyCN: 模型是靠删减造出来的；这个词标出该对象是一种构造物，因此其预测只在删减无碍的范围内成立。

senses.title: Possible in Principle
senses.titleCN: 原则上可能的：逻辑容许
senses.definition: possible according to reasoning, whether or not it can be done in practice
senses.definitionCN: 按推理是可能的，不论实践中能否做到
senses.example: A theoretical solution exists, but nobody can build it yet.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上存在解法，但暂时没人能把它造出来。
senses.why: If the reasoning permits something, it is theoretically possible. The barrier lies in materials or cost, not in logic, which is why the two words 'theoretical' and 'practical' so often face each other.
senses.whyCN: 如果推理容许某件事，它就是理论上可能的；障碍在材料或成本，而不在逻辑，所以 theoretical 与 practical 常常成对出现。

senses.title: Abstract, Not Applied
senses.titleCN: 抽象的：带不务实的意味
senses.definition: concerned with abstract reasoning, often with a hint of impracticality
senses.definitionCN: 关心抽象推理，常暗示不切实际
senses.example: His answer was theoretical and ignored the cost of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答是理论性的，忽略了该计划的成本。
senses.why: When reasoning ignores real conditions, the same word turns mildly critical: correct in the abstract and useless in this room. The tone comes from context, not from the root.
senses.whyCN: 当推理无视现实条件，同一个词就带上轻微批评：抽象上正确，在这间屋子里却没用。这一语气来自语境，而非词根。

senses.title: Consistent within a Theory
senses.titleCN: 理论体系内的：内部自洽
senses.definition: consistent with the definitions and assumptions of a given theory
senses.definitionCN: 与某一理论的定义和假定保持一致
senses.example: The objection is theoretical: the two claims cannot both hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这一反对是理论层面的：两项主张不能同时成立。
senses.why: Inside a theory, statements must fit its own rules. A theoretical objection attacks that fit rather than the data, so it can be settled by argument alone.
senses.whyCN: 在一个理论内部，陈述必须符合它自己的规则；理论性反对攻击的正是这种吻合，而不是数据，因此仅凭论证就能解决。

intro.en: Theoretical descends from Greek theōria 'a looking, contemplation', through Latin theoreticus. The Greek noun is usually traced to theoros 'spectator', but the details of the earliest formation are debated.
intro.cn: theoretical 经拉丁 theoreticus 上溯希腊 theōria「观看、沉思」。这个希腊名词通常追溯到 theoros「观看者」，但最早构词细节仍有争议。

items.en: The noun thea is generally taken to mean 'a view, a sight', and horan means 'to see'. Together they are thought to give theoros, 'one who looks on', especially a spectator at a festival or an envoy consulting an oracle.
items.cn: 名词 thea 一般认为是「景象、观看」，horan 意为「看见」；两者合成 theoros，即「观看的人」，尤指节庆上的观众或去求神谕的使者。此说一般认为是，细节并不完全确定。

items.en: From theoros came the noun theōria, 'the act of looking on, contemplation, a spectacle'. Philosophy borrowed it for the mind's disinterested viewing of truth, away from action.
items.cn: 由 theoros 产生名词 theōria，意为「观看的行为、沉思、景象」。哲学借它指心灵不带功利地观看真理，与行动保持距离。

items.en: Latin took the adjective theorēticus from Greek theoretikos, 'of contemplation'. The Latin form kept the philosophical sense of knowledge pursued for understanding rather than for use.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊 theoretikos 借入形容词 theorēticus，意为「沉思的」。拉丁形式保留了哲学含义：为理解而非为实用而追求的知识。

items.en: English theoretical appears in the seventeenth century beside the older theoretic. The -al form became the everyday adjective, while theoretic survived mainly in fixed academic phrases. The first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 theoretical 于十七世纪出现，与更早的 theoretic 并存。-al 形式成为日常形容词，theoretic 主要残留在固定的学术搭配中。确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: The modern contrast between theoretical and practical is older than English: Greek already opposed theōria to praxis. The pair therefore marks a division of labour, not a judgement that one side is useless.
items.cn: 现代 theoretical 与 practical 的对立比英语更古老：希腊语已用 theōria 对 praxis。因此这一对词标出的是分工，而不是判定某一侧无用。

note.en: The first group traces one Greek family whose members are easily confused. The second holds near-synonyms that sit at different distances from reality.
note.cn: 第一组梳理同一个希腊词族中容易混淆的成员；第二组是距现实远近不同的近义词。

entries.definition: A body of principles that explains a field. It is the thing a theoretical argument is built inside, not the adjective describing the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指解释某一领域的一套原理；理论论证是在它内部进行的，而它不是描述论证的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who builds or studies theory. It names the human agent, so it never replaces theoretical before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指建构或研究理论的人；它命名的是人，因此不能替代名词前的 theoretical。

entries.definition: An older adjective of the same meaning, now mostly confined to phrases such as theoretic framework. It is not a different concept.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的较旧形容词形式，如今多限于 theoretic framework 一类搭配；它并非另一个概念。

entries.definition: Imagined as a premise. It stresses that the case is not real, while theoretical may still describe a well-founded body of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 作为前提被设想出来的；强调情形不真实，而 theoretical 仍可指有根据的推理体系。

entries.definition: Concerning concepts or mental categories. It says the work happens with ideas, not that it is unproven.
entries.definitionCN: 关于概念或心智范畴的；它说的是工作以观念为材料，并不表示未经证实。

entries.definition: General and detached from concrete cases. It can be neutral or critical, but it does not imply a formal theory.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的、脱离具体个案的；可中性也可带批评，但不暗示存在形式化的理论。

entries.definition: Based on conjecture with little evidence. It is more negative than theoretical, which can be rigorous.
entries.definitionCN: 基于猜测而证据不足的；比 theoretical 更负面，因为 theoretical 可以是严谨的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: theoria 'a looking' + -al: knowledge from viewing principles with the mind.
normal.cn: theoria「观看」+ -al：用心灵观看原理而得到的知识。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theorist, theorize, theoretic, theoretical, theorem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 theory、theorist、theorize、theoretic、theoretical、theorem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: theoretical framework, theoretical physics, theoretical model, theoretical possibility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：理论框架、理论物理学、理论模型、理论上的可能性。

normal.en: The opposite pair is theoretical and practical, or theoretical and experimental.
normal.cn: 对立搭配是 theoretical 与 practical，或 theoretical 与 experimental。

normal.en: theorem is a proved statement; theory is the whole system that contains it.
normal.cn: theorem 是被证明的命题；theory 是包含它的整个体系。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn years before anyone walks the ground it describes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，在任何人走过它所描述的地面之前许多年就已画好。

abstract.en: Picture a model ship in a bottle: exact in shape, unable to carry a single passenger.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶中船：形状精确，却载不了一位乘客。

abstract.en: Picture two people arguing about whether a door can open, without ever trying the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人争论一扇门能不能开，却从不去拧门把手。

examples.en: The paper offers a theoretical explanation, but no experiment has tested it.
examples.cn: 这篇论文给出了一种理论解释，但尚无实验检验它。

examples.en: In theoretical terms the plan is sound; in practice it needs money nobody has.
examples.cn: 从理论上说这个计划是成立的；实践中它需要没人拿得出的资金。

examples.en: Students often find theoretical courses dry until they meet a real problem.
examples.cn: 学生常觉得理论课程枯燥，直到遇上一个真实问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: theory（理论）+ etical（形容词词尾）→ 属于理论的 → theoretical 理论的

root: 希腊 thea「景象」+ horan「看见」→ theoros「观看者」→ theōria「观看、沉思」→ 拉丁 theoreticus → 英语 theoretical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with reasoning rather than practice and fan out: a hypothetical case, an unobserved prediction, a branch of a discipline, an idealized model, a logical possibility, an abstract answer and an internal objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「以推理而非实践为本」出发向外展开：假设情形、尚未观测的预言、学科分支、理想化模型、逻辑上的可能、抽象的回答与体系内部的反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formula worked out on a board, separated from the machine it describes.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上推演出的公式，与它所描述的机器之间隔着距离。

branches.en: REASONING APART FROM PRACTICE: knowledge from principles, which can look either rigorous or useless depending on the room.
branches.cn: 与实践分离的推理：来自原理的知识，视场合可显得严谨，也可显得无用。

branches.en: THE SUPPOSED AND THE POSSIBLE: a case invented for argument and a solution the reasoning permits.
branches.cn: 假设与可能：为论证而虚构的情形，以及推理所容许的解法。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN: theory may name a particle before any detector records it.
branches.cn: 未见之物：理论可在任何探测器记录之前先为粒子命名。

branches.en: THE BRANCH: a discipline divides into a theory side and an application side.
branches.cn: 分支：一个学科分为理论侧与应用侧。

branches.en: CONSTRUCTION AND CONSISTENCY: a model built by omission must also stay coherent with its own assumptions.
branches.cn: 构造与自洽：靠省略建成的模型，还必须在自身假定内保持一致。

intro.en: Theoretical is a Greek noun of viewing turned into a Latin adjective and then an English one: root words for sight, a noun ending, and an adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: theoretical 是希腊语中表示「观看」的名词，先转为拉丁形容词，再进入英语：表示视觉的词根、名词词尾，以及形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Greek theōria produced Latin theoreticus and English theory, theoretical, theorist, theorize and theorem. The same sight-root appears in theater, a place for viewing, though that word reached English by a different route.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 theōria 产生拉丁 theoreticus，以及英语 theory、theoretical、theorist、theorize、theorem。同一个「观看」词根也出现在 theater（观看的场所）中，但那个词走的是另一条路径。

items.example: The theoretical part of the course comes first.
items.exampleCN: 课程的理论部分排在前面。

items.meaning: an organized body of explanatory principles
items.meaningCN: 有组织的解释性原理体系
items.example: The theory predicts a slow rise in sea level.
items.exampleCN: 该理论预测海平面会缓慢上升。

items.meaning: one who builds or studies theory
items.example: The theorist never visited the site she wrote about.
items.exampleCN: 这位理论家从未到过她所写的那处遗址。

items.meaning: to form or reason with theories
items.example: They theorized about the cause for years.
items.exampleCN: 他们多年来就成因进行理论推测。

items.meaningCN: theory 的较旧形容词形式
items.exampleCN: 理论研究先于任何测量。

items.structure: theōrēma (a thing viewed, a proposition) + English form
items.example: The theorem holds for every triangle.
items.exampleCN: 该定理对一切三角形都成立。

items.meaning: of the stage; exaggerated as if acted
items.meaningCN: 戏剧的；如表演般夸张的
items.example: His grief was real but theatrical.
items.exampleCN: 他的悲伤是真的，却很戏剧化。

items.example: Theoretically, the bridge can hold twice that load.
items.exampleCN: 理论上，这座桥能承受两倍的荷载。

latinEntries.structure: theōria, -ae (f., first declension, Greek loan in Latin)

latinEntries.meaning: a spectacle; a proposition to be proved
latinEntries.meaningCN: 所见之物；待证明的命题

definition_zh: 设计师；设计者；构思者；名牌的；由设计师设计的
definition_en: a person who plans the form or structure of something before it is made; (of products) made by a famous fashion designer and expensive
core_image: 先在纸上画出蓝图、再动手做出东西的人
scene: 时装周后台一片忙碌，一位年轻的女设计师正在为模特修改裙摆的褶皱。 The designer pinned the hem of the dress minutes before the show began.
sceneCN: 这里 designer 是「设计师」（第 1 个义项：以设计为职业的人）；句意：时装秀开始前几分钟，这位设计师用别针固定了裙摆。

pos.zh: 名牌的；由设计师设计的（如 designer clothes）

collocations.zh: 名牌服装；设计师品牌服装

derivatives.zh: design（基础词）＋ -er（施动者后缀），义为「设计；图样」，是 designer 的词根动词
design 加过去分词形式，义为「经过设计的；有意的」
designed 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「有意地；故意地」
design 加现在分词形式，义为「有预谋的；狡猾的」（常含贬义）
designate（指定）加名词后缀 -ion，义为「指定；命名；头衔」，同源词

senses.title: A person whose job is to plan how something looks or works
senses.definition: a person whose profession is to plan the appearance or structure of things such as clothes, buildings, or machines
senses.definitionCN: 以规划服装、建筑、机器等外观或结构为职业的人
senses.example: The designer of the new bridge won an international prize.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥的设计师获得了国际大奖。
senses.why: The verb design means to plan in advance, so a designer is literally the person who does the planning.
senses.whyCN: 动词 design 意为「预先规划」，-er 表示施动者，designer 就是「做规划的人」，职业义由此而来。

senses.title: A person who invents or plans a scheme or system
senses.titleCN: 构思者；策划者；设计者（非职业义）
senses.definition: a person who thinks out and plans a scheme, a plan, or a system, especially a clever or hidden one
senses.definitionCN: 构思并策划某项计划、方案或体系的人，尤指巧妙的或暗中的设计
senses.example: Historians still argue about whether he was the chief designer of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家仍在争论他是否是这场改革的总策划者。
senses.why: Design once meant any planned scheme, including hidden ones, so the human agent of a scheme keeps this figurative sense.
senses.whyCN: design 早年泛指任何事先谋划的方案，也包括暗中谋划；设计出方案的人因此保留了「策划者」这一引申义。

senses.title: Made by and bearing the name of a famous designer
senses.titleCN: 名牌的；出自设计师品牌的（形容词义）
senses.definition: describing expensive, fashionable products made by a well-known designer and carrying his or her name
senses.definitionCN: 形容出自知名设计师之手、带有其名字的高价时髦产品
senses.example: She only wears designer jeans.
senses.exampleCN: 她只穿名牌牛仔裤。
senses.why: Products once had to be labeled with the designer's name to prove quality, so the noun shifted into an adjective meaning branded.
senses.whyCN: 过去商品要标上设计师的名字才能证明品质，名词因此活用为形容词，表示「带有设计师品牌标签的」。

intro.en: Designer is a Romance-born word: a Latin root passed through French into English, first as a verb, then as a noun of the agent.
intro.cn: designer 是一个源于罗曼语族的词：拉丁词根经法语进入英语，先有动词，再有表施动者的名词。

items.en: The root goes back to Latin designare, from de- (down, out) + signare (to mark), itself from signum (mark, sign).
items.cn: 词根可追溯到拉丁语 designare，由 de-（向下、标出）＋ signare（标记）构成，signare 又出自 signum（记号、符号）。

items.en: The Latin verb passed into Old French as desseigner, meaning to mark out, designate, or plan.
items.cn: 拉丁动词经古法语演变为 desseigner，义为「标出、指明、筹划」。

items.en: English adopted the verb design in the 16th century, at first meaning to mark out or appoint, later to plan and draw in advance.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入动词 design，起初义为「标出、指派」，后转为「预先计划、绘制图样」。

items.en: The noun design appeared in the 17th century, meaning a plan or drawing, and designer followed as the agent noun for the person making such plans.
items.cn: 名词 design 在 17 世纪出现，义为「计划、图样」，随后派生出 designer，指做出这些规划的人。

items.en: From the 20th century, fashion houses made the designer's name a mark of quality, and designer came to be used as an adjective for branded luxury goods.
items.cn: 进入 20 世纪，时装屋让设计师之名成为品质标志，designer 又活用作形容词，指名牌奢侈品。

note.en: The first group collects words that look or sound like designer; the second collects words in the same meaning field of planning and creating.
note.cn: 第一组收集与 designer 形近或音近的词；第二组收集与「规划、创造」同一义场的词。

entries.definition: to officially choose someone or something for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 正式指派、指定；designer 与之同出拉丁 designare 词根

entries.definition: to plan and draw the look or structure of something before it is made
entries.definitionCN: 设计；构思，是 designer 的词根动词

entries.definition: to officially give up a job or position
entries.definitionCN: 辞职；只是拼写与 designer 相近，词源为拉丁 resignare（重新盖章、解除），并无同源关系

entries.definition: a person whose job is to design buildings
entries.definitionCN: 建筑师；专指设计建筑的规划者，与设计师义场相近

entries.definition: a person who makes or brings something into existence
entries.definitionCN: 创造者；强调「造出」而非「预先规划」

entries.definition: a person who makes plans, especially for a city or a project
entries.definitionCN: 规划者；策划人；侧重谋划步骤而非外观造型

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built from the real word family of design.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于 design 真实词族的记忆钩子。

normal.en: design + -er: the -er ending marks the person who does the designing.
normal.cn: design（设计）＋ -er（做……的人）＝做设计的人，即设计师。

normal.en: design itself is de- (down) + sign (mark): to mark out a plan on paper first.
normal.cn: design 来自 de- ＋ sign（记号）：先在纸上把方案「标画出来」。

normal.en: The same root gives designate (to appoint): a designer designates lines and forms.
normal.cn: 同根词 designate（指派）：设计师「指派」每一条线、每一个形。

normal.en: Fashion brand names on a tag: that tag turned designer into an adjective.
normal.cn: 吊牌上的品牌名：正是这个标签让 designer 变成了形容词。「名牌」。

normal.en: Collocations cluster: interior designer, graphic designer, chief designer.
normal.cn: 搭配成串记忆：室内设计师、平面设计师、总设计师。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil sketch becoming a real dress on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铅笔草图最终变成舞台上的一件真裙子。

abstract.en: Imagine signing your own name under your plan, just like a designer labels the product.
abstract.cn: 想象在自己方案下签名，就像设计师把名字标在产品上。

abstract.en: See a blueprint and the finished building side by side.
abstract.cn: 眼前同时出现蓝图与建成的大楼。

examples.en: The designer pinned the hem of the dress minutes before the show began.
examples.cn: 时装秀开始前几分钟，设计师用别针固定了裙摆。

examples.en: He is the chief designer of the city's new subway system.
examples.cn: 他是这座城市新地铁系统的总设计师。

examples.en: Teenagers often dream of owning designer sneakers, though few can afford them.
examples.cn: 青少年常常梦想拥有名牌运动鞋，虽然很少有人买得起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地赛呐」——设计师在「地」图上「赛」着画图，嘴里念念「呐」：比谁的设计更好。读音近似 designer，但谐音只是记忆挂钩，不是词源。

root: designer 来自拉丁语 designare（de- 向下、标出 ＋ signare 标记，signare 源于 signum 记号），经古法语 desseigner 进入英语；动词 design 先行，加施动者后缀 -er 得 designer。

sensesIntro.en: From the professional planner to the agent of any scheme, and finally to the branded product itself, the word drifts from a person to a label.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「职业设计者」到「方案的策划者」，再到商品上的品牌标签，词义从人漂移到标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person who draws the plan before the thing exists
core.cn: 核心意象：在东西造出来之前，先把方案画出来的人

branches.en: The profession sense: designer as job title.
branches.cn: 职业义：designer 作为头衔——设计师。

branches.en: The scheme sense: designer as mastermind behind a plan.
branches.cn: 谋划义：designer 指幕后策划者、总设计师。

branches.en: The bridge from person to product: the designer's name becomes the brand.
branches.cn: 从人到物的桥梁：设计师之名变成品牌。

branches.en: The adjective sense: designer goods as status symbols.
branches.cn: 形容词义：designer 商品成为身份象征。

branches.en: All three senses share one core: someone deliberately shapes what others will see.
branches.cn: 三个义项共享一个内核：有人刻意塑造别人将要看到的东西。

intro.en: Designer is built with simple, transparent pieces: a Latin prefix, a Latin root, and an English agent suffix.
intro.cn: designer 由简单透明的部件构成：一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁词根和一个英语施动者后缀。

latinIntro.en: The root sign- (mark) is one of the most productive Latin roots in English.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 sign-（记号）是英语中最能产的拉丁词根之一。

the act of designating; a title
items.example: the designation of a new chairman

items.meaning: a person's name written by himself

latinEntries.meaning: to mark, to set a sign upon

definition_zh: 普遍的；全体的；通用的；宇宙的
definition_en: true of or shared by everyone or everything, or able to be used in all cases
core_image: 一张巨大的圆顶把天南地北的人与物全罩在里面，没有一处露在边缘之外
scene: 孩子们在课堂上争论笑容是不是人人都懂，老师让全班用自己的语言演示同一个表情。 Smiling appears to be universal across every culture.
sceneCN: 这里 universal 是「普遍的、人人都有的」（第 1 个义项：对所有人都成立）；句意为微笑似乎在所有文化中都是普遍的。罩住一切的那个圆顶，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 普遍的；全体的；人人都有的
普遍概念；通用规律（哲学用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；人人皆然地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「普遍性；通用性」
与本词同源，义为「宇宙；全体」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指师生的全体团体

senses.title: True of everyone
senses.definition: applying to or shared by all people or all things of a kind
senses.definitionCN: 适用于某类的所有人或所有事物，或为其所共有
senses.example: The desire for safety is universal among parents.
senses.exampleCN: 对安全的渴望在父母心中是普遍的。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned towards one: the whole field is gathered into a single reach.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「朝向一个」：整片领域被收进同一个范围。

senses.title: Usable in all cases
senses.definition: designed to work or apply in every case, without special adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别调整即可在任何情形下使用或适用
senses.example: A universal charger saves travellers from carrying five cables.
senses.exampleCN: 一只通用充电器让旅客不必带五根线。
senses.why: The adjective extends from people to tools: one form that fits everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从人扩展到工具：一种形式适合一切。

senses.title: Of the whole universe
senses.definition: relating to the whole of space and everything in it
senses.definitionCN: 与整个空间及其中的一切有关的
senses.example: Gravity is a universal force, acting on every mass in space.
senses.exampleCN: 引力是一种宇宙之力，作用于太空中的每个质量。
senses.why: In philosophy the word already meant the whole of things, and astronomy borrowed that reach.
senses.whyCN: 在哲学中这个词本已指万物的全体，天文学借用了这份范围。

senses.title: A general concept
senses.definition: in philosophy, a quality or concept said of many things rather than of one
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指可被多个事物共有的性质或概念，而非单个事物
senses.example: Medieval thinkers argued about whether universals exist apart from things.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪思想家争论普遍概念是否存在于事物之外。
senses.why: Logic needs a name for what many share, and the word for whole becomes that name.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要为众多事物共有之物命名，表示「全体」的词就成了这个名字。

senses.title: Everyone, without exception
senses.titleCN: 全体一致的；无一例外的
senses.definition: in phrases such as universal approval, agreeing by all without a single objection
senses.definitionCN: 在 universal approval 等说法中，指全体同意、没有一票反对
senses.example: The new playground won universal approval at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新游乐场在会上获得一致赞同。
senses.why: Here the word does not describe a law but counts people: nobody is left outside.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不描述规律而在数人：没有一个人被留在外面。

intro.en: Universal is built on the same Latin pair as universe: one, and turning towards one whole.
intro.cn: universal 与 universe 建立在同一对拉丁语词上：「一」，以及「转向同一整体」。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the verb vertere meant to turn; the pair gave universus, turned into one, whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，动词 vertere 意为「转动」；二者合出 universus，即「合成一个、整个的」。

items.en: Late Latin universalis meant belonging to all, and it was the adjective used in logic and law.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 universalis 意为「属于全体的」，是逻辑学与法学里的形容词。

items.en: French universal carried the sense of general and applied to all cases.
items.cn: 法语 universal 带有「一般的、适用于一切情形」的意思。

items.en: Scholastic writers used universal for concepts shared by many things.
items.cn: 经院作者用 universal 指众多事物共有的概念。

items.en: Natural science took up the word for laws holding everywhere, and everyday speech took it for what everyone shares.
items.cn: 自然科学取它表示处处成立的定律，日常言语则取它表示人人共有之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of scope with different breadth.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示范围的形容词，宽窄不同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by everyone or in every case.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「普遍地、人人皆然地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of applying to all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍性、通用性」。

entries.definition: Everything that exists, literally turned into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，字面即「合为一体」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning, once a whole community of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体团体。

entries.definition: The belief that a principle holds for everyone everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍主义」，认为某原则对天下所有人成立。

entries.definition: True in most cases but allowing exceptions; weaker than universal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一般的」，多数情形成立但允许例外，比 universal 弱。

entries.definition: Covering the whole world in space or reach.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全球的」，指在空间或影响上覆盖整个世界。

entries.definition: Found over a large area or among many people, but not necessarily all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的」，地域或人群范围大，但不一定涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Shared by many or occurring often; it makes no claim about everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「共同的、常见的」，不主张对人人成立。

entries.definition: Broad in taste or interest, or universal in the older sense; formal and rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的、普遍的」，较正式而少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and turn, and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「转」，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is to turn: turned into one, so everything is inside.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：转成一整个，所以一切都在里面。

normal.en: A universal truth holds for everyone, without exceptions.
normal.cn: 普遍真理对每人都成立，没有例外。

normal.en: A universal charger replaces a bag of cables.
normal.cn: 通用充电器能替掉一包线。

normal.en: University and universe share the root: one whole of students, one whole of things.
normal.cn: university 与 universe 共享词根：学生的整体，与万物的整体。

normal.en: Universal approval means not one hand stayed down.
normal.cn: 一致赞同意味着没有一只手没举起来。

abstract.en: Picture a dome wide enough to cover every town at once: whatever stands outside it is, by definition, an exception.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽到能同时罩住每座城镇的圆顶：站在外面的事物按定义就是例外。

abstract.en: To call a rule universal is a strong claim; one counterexample is enough to break it.
abstract.cn: 称一条规律为普遍的是很强的断言：一个反例就足以打破它。

abstract.en: The word gathers a whole world into one turning point, which is why it can cover laws and people alike.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一整个世界收进同一个转折点，因此它既能盖住规律，也能盖住人。

examples.en: Music is often called a universal language.
examples.cn: 音乐常被称为一种通用语言。

examples.en: Access to clean water should be a universal right.
examples.cn: 获得干净的水应当是一项普遍权利。

examples.en: The plan met with universal support at the council meeting.
examples.cn: 这项计划在议会上得到了全体支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃索」——优尼把沃索全部转进一个圈：普遍的、全体的

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，晚期拉丁语 universalis「属于全体的」经法语进入英语；由「全体」引申出普遍、通用与宇宙等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universal all describe one reach: a whole gathered into one, whether it is all people, all cases, all of space, a shared concept, or a vote without exception.
sensesIntro.cn: universal 的五个义项都描述同一种覆盖：把整体收成一个，无论那是所有人、所有情形、整个空间、共有概念，还是无一例外的表决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome that encloses every place and leaves nothing outside.

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: a feeling or truth shared by everyone.

branches.en: THE TOOL: one design that fits every case.
branches.cn: 工具线：一种设计适用于每一种情形。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: the reach extends to all of space.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：覆盖范围扩展到整个空间。

branches.en: THE CONCEPT: philosophy names what many things share.
branches.cn: 概念线：哲学为众多事物共有之物命名。

branches.en: THE VOTE: nobody is left outside the agreement.
branches.cn: 表决线：没有人被留在同意之外。

definition_zh: 持有人；持有者；支架；托架；夹具
definition_en: a person who owns or has something such as a ticket or a title, or an object used to hold something in place
core_image: 握住不放的手：证件、头衔被握在手里，笔被卡在托架上
scene: 图书馆的借阅台上，管理员把卡片递还给他，说了一句。 The library clerk handed back the card and said, "Show it to the holder at the front desk."
sceneCN: 这里 holder 是「持有人」（第 1 个义项：合法持有某物的人）；句意是管理员让他把卡片出示给前台那位持有它的人，核心画面是把东西握在手里的人。

pos.zh: 持有人；持有者（证件、头衔、职务等）
支架；托架；夹具（固定物品的器具）

hold 加 -ing 构成，义为「持有；持有的股份或产业」
house 与 hold 复合，义为「家庭；一家人」

senses.title: A person who legally has something
senses.definition: a person who owns, possesses, or officially has something such as a ticket, a card, or an account
senses.definitionCN: 合法拥有或持有票证、卡片、账户等东西的人
senses.example: Ticket holders should arrive thirty minutes early.
senses.exampleCN: 持票人应提前三十分钟到场。
senses.why: The verb hold means to keep something in your hands, so a holder is simply the person on the other side of that hand.
senses.whyCN: 动词 hold 表示「握住」，holder 就是「握着它的人」，从手上的动作落到人的身份上。

senses.title: A person who holds a title, record, or position
senses.definition: a person who has a title, a record, an office, or a position
senses.definitionCN: 拥有头衔、保持纪录或担任某一职务的人
senses.example: She is the world record holder in the marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 她是马拉松世界纪录保持者。
senses.why: A title or record is imagined as something grasped and not let go, so the person keeping it is the holder.
senses.whyCN: 头衔和纪录被想象成「握在手里不放」的东西，谁握着谁就是 holder。

senses.title: An object used to hold something in place
senses.definition: a device or container designed to keep an object steady or in position
senses.definitionCN: 用来固定或安放物品的器具，使其稳定不动
senses.example: There is a cup holder beside each seat in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车内每个座位旁边都有一个杯架。
senses.why: The core image of holding extends from people to tools: the device literally holds the object for you.
senses.whyCN: 「握住」的意象从人扩展到器具：这种装置替你「握住」物品，于是也叫 holder。

intro.en: Holder is a transparent English formation: the verb hold plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: holder 是一个构成透明的英语词：动词 hold 加上表「人／物」的后缀 -er。

items.en: The verb goes back to the reconstructed Proto-Germanic root *haldan or *huldan, meaning to keep or to grasp.
items.cn: 动词可追溯至重构的原始日耳曼语词根 *haldan／*huldan，意为「保存；抓住」。

items.en: In Old English it appears as healdan, meaning to contain, to keep, or to guard.
items.cn: 古英语写作 healdan，表示「容纳；保有；守护」。

items.en: The verb settles as holden, and the agent noun holder emerges with the -er suffix.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 holden，带 -er 后缀的施动名词 holder 随之出现。

items.en: The personal sense, one who has a title or a document, becomes common in legal and commercial writing.
items.cn: 表示「持有文件、头衔之人」的用法在十六至十七世纪的法律与商业文书中普及。

items.en: The object sense, a device that holds something, spreads with everyday inventions such as pen holders and match holders.
items.cn: 十九世纪随笔架、火柴座等日常小物件的普及，「固定物品的器具」一义广泛使用。

items.en: Today holder freely combines with other nouns: ticket holder, account holder, cup holder.
items.cn: 如今 holder 可自由与名词组合：ticket holder 持票人、account holder 账户持有人、cup holder 杯架。

note.en: Holder looks plain, but it hides two near neighbours with different suffixes and a small family of look-alikes.
note.cn: holder 看似简单，但它有两个后缀相近的邻居，还有一小群拼写相像的词。

entries.definitionCN: 所有者；物主，强调所有权而非 merely 持有

entries.definition: a person who has or owns something, often in legal contexts
entries.definitionCN: 占有人；持有人，正式用语，常见于法律语境

entries.definition: a person who takes care of or guards something
entries.definitionCN: 保管人；看守人，侧重「看管」而非「持有」

entries.definition: a device attached to a wall to hold or support something
entries.definitionCN: 托架；支架，与 holder 第 3 义项相近

entries.definition: a person who holds property or land by renting it

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built from the real root hold and its real combinations.
normalIntro.cn: 五条锚点，全部基于真实的词根 hold 及其真实组合。

normal.en: hold + -er: the one who holds is the holder.
normal.cn: hold 加 -er：握着的人就是「持有者」。

normal.en: Ticket holder: the ticket is in that person's hand.
normal.cn: 持票人：票就攥在那个人手里。

normal.en: Record holder: the record has never been let go.
normal.cn: 纪录保持者：纪录一直被「握住」没被打破。

normal.en: Cup holder: the little device holds your cup steady.
normal.cn: 杯架：替你「握住」水杯的小装置。

normal.en: Account holder: the bank account belongs to this person.
normal.cn: 账户持有人：银行账户就记在这人名下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never opens: whatever it grips makes its owner a holder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永不松开的手：握住什么，它主人就是什么 holder。

abstract.en: A trophy on a shelf is held by a bracket, just as a title is held by a person.
abstract.cn: 架上的奖杯被托架「握」着，头衔被人在「握」着，画面相通。

abstract.en: From gripping hands to gripping tools, the idea of steady holding never changes.
abstract.cn: 从握紧的手到咬合的卡扣，「稳稳握住」这一个意象贯穿所有义项。

examples.en: The account holder must sign the form in person.
examples.cn: 账户持有人必须亲自在这份表格上签字。

examples.en: Every seat in the new car has a cup holder.
examples.cn: 新车的每个座位都配有杯架。

examples.en: She became the record holder after swimming the fastest lap.
examples.cn: 游出最快一圈之后，她成了纪录保持者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厚的」——想象一张很厚的大存折，握在谁手里，谁就是持有人（holder）。

root: holder 由动词 hold（握住；持有）加施动者后缀 -er 构成，属古英语本族词。hold 可追溯至重构的原始日耳曼语词根 *haldan／*huldan，一般认为与「看守、容纳」义相关；与拉丁词根无亲缘关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hand that does not let go: it points to a person holding a document or title, and then to a device holding an object.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一只不松开的手：先指向握着证件或头衔的人，再延伸到固定物品的器具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady grip, held by a person or by a device
core.cn: 核心意象：一次稳定的握持，可以出自人手，也可以出自器具

branches.en: the hand on a ticket or card makes that person the holder
branches.cn: 握着票证的那只手，让人成为持有人

branches.en: a title or record is imagined as something gripped and never released
branches.cn: 头衔与纪录被想象成握住不放的东西

branches.en: both personal senses share the idea of lawful keeping
branches.cn: 两个「人」的义项共享「合法保有」的观念

branches.en: the device sense appears when the holder is a bracket or tray
branches.cn: 当握持者变成托架或卡座，就长出器具义

branches.en: keeping a title and fixing an object both rest on the same steady grip
branches.cn: 保持头衔与固定物品，都立足于同一次稳定的握持

intro.en: Holder is built from a native English verb plus the most productive agent suffix in the language.
intro.cn: holder 由英语本族动词加英语里最高产的施动者后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -er is Germanic, not Latin, but Latin uses -or for the same job; the pairs below show the parallel.

senses.title: The great evil spirit

senses.example: The old story says the devil lives under the bridge.

senses.why: A village needs one face to put on everything it fears.

intro.en: Devil comes from Greek diabolos, a slanderer, through Latin diabolus and Old English deofol.
intro.cn: devil 来自希腊语 diabolos（诽谤者），经拉丁语 diabolus 与古英语 deofol 进入英语。

items.en: Diabolos meant a slanderer, one who throws words across to divide people.
items.cn: diabolos 指诽谤者，即把话扔过去让人分裂的人。

items.en: Latin diabolus took the word over as the name of the chief evil spirit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diabolus 接过这个词，用作首要恶灵的名字。

items.en: Deofol entered English with Christian teaching.
items.cn: deofol 随基督教教义进入英语。

items.en: The word spread into curses, proverbs and everyday scolding.
items.cn: 这个词扩展进咒骂、谚语与日常责骂里。

items.en: It now also teases a naughty child or pities a poor man.
items.cn: 如今它也用来打趣淘气的孩子，或同情可怜的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the devil stem or sound, and the meaning group names evil spirits.
note.cn: 形近组共用 devil 的词干或读音，近义组则指各种邪恶精灵。

entries.definition: like a devil, or very difficult

normal.en: The Greek word meant slanderer, so the devil began as a whisperer.

normal.en: One word carries both the terror and the teasing.

normal.en: A poor devil is a man whose luck has run out.
normal.cn: a poor devil 就是运气用光了的男人。

normal.en: The devil in a story always arrives with a bargain.
normal.cn: 故事里的魔鬼，总是带着一桩交易上场。

normal.en: Small horns on a child are only a costume.
normal.cn: 孩子头上的小角，不过是一套装扮。

abstract.en: Picture a hand offering a contract across a table.

abstract.en: Picture keys hidden under a cushion.

examples.en: The old story says the devil lives under the bridge.

examples.en: The poor devil had lost his home and his job.
examples.cn: 那个可怜的家伙失去了房子和工作。

examples.en: You little devil, you hid my keys again.
examples.cn: 你这个小淘气，又把我的钥匙藏起来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devil 记成「得我」：de 是向下，vil 像「歪」，心思一路向下歪，就成了魔鬼。

root: 来自希腊语 diabolos（诽谤者、挑拨者），经拉丁语 diabolus 与古英语 deofol 进入英语。本义是宗教中的首要恶灵，后来用于骂人、表示恶棍，也用来打趣淘气的孩子或同情处境可怜的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a spirit that whispers division, to a man whose luck has failed, to a small child with a grin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从低声挑拨的灵，到运气耗尽的人，再到咧嘴笑的小孩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horned shadow thrown on a wall by firelight.
core.cn: 核心意象：火光在墙上投下一个带角的影子。

branches.en: The first sense is the shadow that religion gave a name.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是宗教给了名字的那个影子。

branches.en: The second sense turns that name onto a man who suffers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这个名字转到受苦的人身上。

branches.en: The third sense shrinks the horns to toy size.

branches.en: The great evil and an ordinary wretch share one word.

senses.title: A multi-lane road for fast motor traffic

senses.title: The motorway as a British institution
senses.definition: the motorway network as a whole, referred to when talking about driving, congestion, or road works
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的高速公路网络，谈论驾车、拥堵或道路施工时提到
senses.example: Road works on the motorway added an hour to every journey that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天高速公路上的道路施工让每趟车都多花一小时。
senses.why: Once the roads had a name of their own, the name came to stand for the whole network and the shared experience of driving on it.
senses.whyCN: 当这类道路有了自己的名字，这个名字便开始指代整个路网，以及在上面开车的那份共同经历。

intro.en: Motorway is a straightforward English compound of motor and way, coined in the early twentieth century when Britain began building roads reserved for motor vehicles.
intro.cn: motorway 是 motor 与 way 构成的直白英语复合词，二十世纪初英国开始修建机动车专用道路时被造出来。

items.en: Movere meant to move, and motor, its agent noun, named the thing that sets others moving.
items.cn: movere 意为移动，其施动名词 motor 指让别的东西动起来的那一方。

items.en: Via was the Latin word for a road or way, the notion English later expressed with its Germanic word way.
items.cn: via 是拉丁语里「道路」一词，英语后来用日耳曼语源的 way 表达同一概念。

items.en: English had long made compounds like railway and carriageway, so motorway followed a familiar pattern once motor traffic existed.
items.cn: 英语早有 railway、carriageway 这类复合词，一旦机动车出现，motorway 便顺着这个熟悉的模式被造出来。

items.en: Britain opened its first purpose-built motorway in 1958, and the word settled into everyday use with the new roads.
items.cn: 英国于 1958 年开通第一条专用高速公路，这个词随新路一道进入日常用语。

items.en: Modern English keeps motorway as the standard British term; American English prefers freeway or expressway for the same kind of road.
items.cn: 现代英语中 motorway 是标准英式说法；美式英语对同类道路更常用 freeway 或 expressway。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built on motor or way; the near-meaning group gathers the other words English uses for high-speed roads.
note.cn: 形近组收以 motor 或 way 构成的复合词；近义组收英语里表示高速道路的其他说法。

entries.definition: A machine that turns energy into movement, or a car in British informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量变成运动的机器，英式口语中也指汽车。

entries.definition: A person who drives a motor vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶机动车的人。

entries.definition: A road of rails on which trains run; built with the same way compound but for trains.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶的轨道线路；与 motorway 共用 way 的复合方式，但服务于火车。

entries.definition: The usual American name for a wide multi-lane road without crossings.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语对无平面交叉多车道宽路的常用称呼。

entries.definition: Another American term for a fast urban or intercity road.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语对快速城市或城际道路的另一种称呼。

entries.definition: A general word for a main public road; broader than motorway, which names the special fast class.
entries.definitionCN: 对干线公路的统称；比 motorway 含义更宽，后者专指那类特殊的高速道路。

normalIntro.en: The word says what it is: a way reserved for motors, and the family around it follows the same plain pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把自身说清楚了：一条留给 motor（机动车）的路，它周围的词族也遵循同样直白的构词方式。

normal.en: Motorway is motor plus way, literally a road for motor vehicles, with nothing hidden in the compound.
normal.cn: motorway 是 motor 加 way，字面就是「机动车走的路」，复合词里没有任何隐藏含义。

normal.en: Compare railway: the same word way is used, only the vehicle changes, rail for trains and motor for cars.
normal.cn: 对比 railway：用的是同一个 way，只是交通工具换了——rail 给火车，motor 给汽车。

normal.en: Motorist and motorway share the same base, so the driver and the road both belong to the motor family.
normal.cn: motorist 与 motorway 共用同一个基础词，驾车者和这条路都归在 motor 词族之下。

normal.en: Freeway, expressway and motorway all end in way, which is English's favorite ending for a named class of road.
normal.cn: freeway、expressway、motorway 都以 way 结尾，这是英语给各类道路命名时最爱的词尾。

normal.en: British usage reserves motorway for the special grade-separated roads, so the word is narrower than highway.
normal.cn: 英式用法里 motorway 专指立体交叉的特殊道路，因此它比 highway 的范围窄。

abstract.en: Picture two unbroken ribbons of headlights flowing in opposite directions, nothing crossing them.
abstract.cn: 想象两条不间断的车灯光带朝相反方向流动，没有任何东西横穿其间。

abstract.en: A road named after the vehicle it carries is a small lesson in how English compounds describe function.
abstract.cn: 一条以它所承载的交通工具命名的路，正是英语复合词按功能描述事物的小小例证。

abstract.en: The word is at its most itself when seen from above: lanes, slip roads, and nothing that walks across.
abstract.cn: 从空中俯瞰时这个词最像它自己：车道、匝道，以及绝无横穿的行人。

examples.en: They joined the motorway and covered two hundred miles before dark.
examples.cn: 他们驶上高速公路，天黑前跑了两百英里。

examples.en: Road works on the motorway added an hour to every journey that summer.
examples.cn: 那年夏天高速公路上的道路施工让每趟车都多花一小时。

examples.en: Drivers must not stop on the hard shoulder unless it is an emergency.
examples.cn: 除非紧急情况，司机不得在紧急停车带上停车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托喂」——摩托车和汽车都要「喂」油才能上这条路；motorway 就是机动车专用的高速公路。

root: 英语复合词：motor（源于拉丁语 movere「移动」的施动名词 motor「推动者」）+ way（源于古英语 weg「道路」），义为「供机动车行驶的道路」。

sensesIntro.en: The compound names a road by the vehicles built for it; the senses move from a single stretch of road to the network as an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 复合词按所服务的车辆给道路命名；义项从一段具体的路延伸到作为整体的路网。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several lanes flowing one way, cut off from everything that walks or crosses.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条车道朝一个方向奔流，与一切横穿的行人车辆隔绝。

branches.en: headlights streaming along lanes in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗中沿车道奔涌的车灯

branches.en: a slip road curving up to join the main carriageway
branches.cn: 弯上去汇入主车道的匝道

branches.en: a bridge carrying a farm track over the lanes
branches.cn: 让田间小路跨过车道的天桥

branches.en: a service station full of travelers at midnight
branches.cn: 午夜挤满旅客的服务区

branches.en: orange cones and speed limits through road works
branches.cn: 施工路段的橙色路锥与限速牌

intro.en: Motorway is a pure compound: a Latin-derived noun for the engine vehicle joined to an Old English word for road.
intro.cn: motorway 是纯粹的复合词：一个源自拉丁语、指发动机车辆的名词，加上一个源自古英语、指道路的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin side of the family comes from movere and its agent noun motor; the way side comes from Germanic, so the compound joins two language streams.
latinIntro.cn: 词族的拉丁语一侧来自 movere 及其施动名词 motor；way 一侧来自日耳曼语源，这个复合词把两条语言源流接在了一起。
